chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: dhåtaräñöra uväca dharma-kñetre kuru-kñetre samavetä yuyutsavaù mämakäù päëòaväç caiva kim akurvata saïjaya
transliteration: dhataranora uvaca dharma-knetre kuru-knetre samaveta yuyutsavau mamakau paeoavac caiva kim akurvata saijaya
translation: Dhåtaräñöra said: O Saïjaya, after assembling in the place of pilgrimage at Kurukñetra, what did my sons and the sons of Päëòu do, being desirous to fight?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: saïjaya uväca dåñövä tu päëòavänékaà vyüòhaà duryodhanas tadä äcäryam upasaìgamya räjä vacanam abravét
transliteration: saijaya uvaca danova tu paeoavanekaa vyuohaa duryodhanas tada acaryam upasaigamya raja vacanam abravet
translation: Saïjaya said: O King, after looking over the army gathered by the sons of Päëòu, King Duryodhana went to his teacher and began to speak the following words:
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: paçyaitäà päëòu-puträëäm äcärya mahatéà camüm vyüòhäà drupada-putreëa tava çiñyeëa dhématä
transliteration: pacyaitaa paeou-putraeam acarya mahatea camum vyuohaa drupada-putreea tava cinyeea dhemata
translation: O my teacher, behold the great army of the sons of Päëòu, so expertly arranged by your intelligent disciple, the son of Drupada.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: atra çürä maheñv-äsä bhémärjuna-samä yudhi yuyudhäno viräöaç ca drupadaç ca mahä-rathaù
transliteration: atra cura mahenv-asa bhemarjuna-sama yudhi yuyudhano viraoac ca drupadac ca maha-rathau
translation: Here in this army there are many heroic bowmen equal in fighting to Bhéma and Arjuna; there are also great fighters like Yuyudhäna, Viräöa and Drupada.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: dhåñöaketuç cekitänaù käçiräjaç ca véryavän purujit kuntibhojaç ca çaibyaç ca nara-puìgavaù
transliteration: dhanoaketuc cekitanau kacirajac ca veryavan purujit kuntibhojac ca caibyac ca nara-puigavau
translation: There are also great, heroic, powerful fighters like Dhåñöaketu, Cekitäna, Käçiräja, Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Çaibya.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: yudhämanyuç ca vikränta uttamaujäç ca véryavän saubhadro draupadeyäç ca sarva eva mahä-rathäù
transliteration: yudhamanyuc ca vikranta uttamaujac ca veryavan saubhadro draupadeyac ca sarva eva maha-rathau
translation: There are the mighty Yudhämanyu, the very powerful Uttamaujä, the son of Subhadrä and the sons of Draupadé. All these warriors are great chariot fighters.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: asmäkaà tu viçiñöä ye tän nibodha dvijottama näyakä mama sainyasya saàjïärthaà tän bravémi te
transliteration: asmakaa tu vicinoa ye tan nibodha dvijottama nayaka mama sainyasya saajiarthaa tan bravemi te
translation: O best of the brähmaëas, for your information, let me tell you about the captains who are especially qualified to lead my military force.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: bhavän bhéñmaç ca karëaç ca kåpaç ca samitià-jayaù açvatthämä vikarëaç ca saumadattis tathaiva ca
transliteration: bhavan bhenmac ca kareac ca kapac ca samitia-jayau acvatthama vikareac ca saumadattis tathaiva ca
translation: There are personalities like yourself, Bhéñma, Karëa, Kåpa, Açvatthämä, Vikarëa and the son of Somadatta called Bhuriçravä, who are always victorious in battle.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: anye ca bahavaù çürä mad-arthe tyakta-jévitäù nänä-çastra-praharaëäù sarve yuddha-viçäradäù
transliteration: anye ca bahavau cura mad-arthe tyakta-jevitau nana-castra-praharaeau sarve yuddha-vicaradau
translation: There are many other heroes who are prepared to lay down their lives for my sake. All of them are well equipped with different kinds of weapons, and all are experienced in military science.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: aparyäptaà tad asmäkaà balaà bhéñmäbhirakñitam paryäptaà tv idam eteñäà balaà bhémäbhirakñitam
transliteration: aparyaptaa tad asmakaa balaa bhenmabhiraknitam paryaptaa tv idam etenaa balaa bhemabhiraknitam
translation: Our strength is immeasurable, and we are perfectly protected by Grandfather Bhéñma, whereas the strength of the Päëòavas, carefully protected by Bhéma, is limited.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: ayaneñu ca sarveñu yathä-bhägam avasthitäù bhéñmam eväbhirakñantu bhavantaù sarva eva hi
transliteration: ayanenu ca sarvenu yatha-bhagam avasthitau bhenmam evabhiraknantu bhavantau sarva eva hi
translation: Now all of you must give full support to Grandfather Bhéñma, standing at your respective strategic points in the phalanx of the army.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: tasya saïjanayan harñaà kuru-våddhaù pitämahaù siàha-nädaà vinadyoccaiù çaìkhaà dadhmau pratäpavän
transliteration: tasya saijanayan harnaa kuru-vaddhau pitamahau siaha-nadaa vinadyoccaiu caikhaa dadhmau pratapavan
translation: Then Bhéñma, the great valiant grandsire of the Kuru dynasty, the grandfather of the fighters, blew his conchshell very loudly like the sound of a lion, giving Duryodhana joy.

glossary.gloss: the grandsire of the Kuru dynasty (Bhéñma)

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: tataù çaìkhäç ca bheryaç ca paëavänaka-gomukhäù sahasaiväbhyahanyanta sa çabdas tumulo ’bhavat
transliteration: tatau caikhac ca bheryac ca paeavanaka-gomukhau sahasaivabhyahanyanta sa cabdas tumulo 'bhavat
translation: After that, the conchshells, bugles, trumpets, drums and horns were all suddenly sounded, and the combined sound was tumultuous.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: tataù çvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau mädhavaù päëòavaç caiva divyau çaìkhau pradadhmatuù
transliteration: tatau cvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau madhavau paeoavac caiva divyau caikhau pradadhmatuu
translation: On the other side, both Lord Kåñëa and Arjuna, stationed on a great chariot drawn by white horses, sounded their transcendental conchshells.

glossary.gloss: Kåñëa (the husband of the goddess of fortune)

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: päïcajanyaà håñékeço devadattaà dhanaïjayaù pauëòraà dadhmau mahä-çaìkhaà bhéma-karmä våkodaraù
transliteration: paicajanyaa hanekeco devadattaa dhanaijayau paueoraa dadhmau maha-caikhaa bhema-karma vakodarau
translation: Then, Lord Kåñëa blew His conchshell, called Päïcajanya; Arjuna blew his, the Devadatta; and Bhéma, the voracious eater and performer of Herculean tasks, blew his terrific conchshell called Pauëòram.

glossary.gloss: Håñékeça (Kåñëa, the Lord who directs the senses of the devotees)

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: anantavijayaà räjä kunté-putro yudhiñöhiraù nakulaù sahadevaç ca sughoña-maëipuñpakau
transliteration: anantavijayaa raja kunte-putro yudhinohirau nakulau sahadevac ca sughona-maeipunpakau
translation: King Yudhiñöhira, the son of Kunté, blew his conchshell, the Anantavijaya, and Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughoña and Maëipuñpaka. That great archer the King of Käçé, the great fighter Çikhaëòé, Dhåñöadyumna, Viräöa and the unconquerable Sätyaki, Drupada, the sons of Draupadé, and the others, O King, such as the son of Subhadrä, greatly armed, all blew their respective conchshells.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: käçyaç ca parameñv-äsaù çikhaëòé ca mahä-rathaù dhåñöadyumno viräöaç ca sätyakiç cäparäjitaù
transliteration: kacyac ca paramenv-asau cikhaeoe ca maha-rathau dhanoadyumno viraoac ca satyakic caparajitau
translation: King Yudhiñöhira, the son of Kunté, blew his conchshell, the Anantavijaya, and Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughoña and Maëipuñpaka. That great archer the King of Käçé, the great fighter Çikhaëòé, Dhåñöadyumna, Viräöa and the unconquerable Sätyaki, Drupada, the sons of Draupadé, and the others, O King, such as the son of Subhadrä, greatly armed, all blew their respective conchshells.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: drupado draupadeyäç ca sarvaçaù påthivé-pate saubhadraç ca mahä-bähuù çaìkhän dadhmuù påthak påthak
transliteration: drupado draupadeyac ca sarvacau pathive-pate saubhadrac ca maha-bahuu caikhan dadhmuu pathak pathak
translation: King Yudhiñöhira, the son of Kunté, blew his conchshell, the Anantavijaya, and Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughoña and Maëipuñpaka. That great archer the King of Käçé, the great fighter Çikhaëòé, Dhåñöadyumna, Viräöa and the unconquerable Sätyaki, Drupada, the sons of Draupadé, and the others, O King, such as the son of Subhadrä, greatly armed, all blew their respective conchshells.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: sa ghoño dhärtaräñöräëäà hådayäni vyadärayat nabhaç ca påthivéà caiva tumulo ’bhyanunädayan
transliteration: sa ghono dhartaranoraeaa hadayani vyadarayat nabhac ca pathivea caiva tumulo 'bhyanunadayan
translation: The blowing of these different conchshells became uproarious, and thus, vibrating both in the sky and on the earth, it shattered the hearts of the sons of Dhåtaräñöra.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: atha vyavasthitän dåñövä dhärtaräñörän kapi-dhvajaù pravåtte çastra-sampäte dhanur udyamya päëòavaù håñékeçaà tadä väkyam idam äha mahé-pate
transliteration: atha vyavasthitan danova dhartaranoran kapi-dhvajau pravatte castra-sampate dhanur udyamya paeoavau hanekecaa tada vakyam idam aha mahe-pate
translation: O King, at that time Arjuna, the son of Päëòu, who was seated in his chariot, his flag marked with Hanumän, took up his bow and prepared to shoot his arrows, looking at the sons of Dhåtaräñöra. O King, Arjuna then spoke to Håñékeça [Kåñëa] these words:

glossary.gloss: one whose flag is marked with Hanumän

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: arjuna uväca senayor ubhayor madhye rathaà sthäpaya me ’cyuta yävad etän nirékñe ’haà
transliteration: arjuna uvaca senayor ubhayor madhye rathaa sthapaya me 'cyuta yavad etan nirekne 'haa
translation: Arjuna said: O infallible one, please draw my chariot between the two armies so that I may see who is present here, who is desirous of fighting, and with whom I must contend in this great battle attempt.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: yoddhu-kämän avasthitän kair mayä saha yoddhavyam asmin raëa-samudyame
transliteration: yoddhu-kaman avasthitan kair maya saha yoddhavyam asmin raea-samudyame
translation: Arjuna said: O infallible one, please draw my chariot between the two armies so that I may see who is present here, who is desirous of fighting, and with whom I must contend in this great battle attempt.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: yotsyamänän avekñe ’haà ya ete ’tra samägatäù dhärtaräñörasya durbuddher yuddhe priya-cikérñavaù
transliteration: yotsyamanan avekne 'haa ya ete 'tra samagatau dhartaranorasya durbuddher yuddhe priya-cikernavau
translation: Let me see those who have come here to fight, wishing to please the evilminded son of Dhåtaräñöra.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: saïjaya uväca evam ukto håñékeço guòäkeçena bhärata senayor ubhayor madhye sthäpayitvä rathottamam
transliteration: saijaya uvaca evam ukto hanekeco guoakecena bharata senayor ubhayor madhye sthapayitva rathottamam
translation: Saïjaya said: O descendant of Bharata, being thus addressed by Arjuna, Lord Kåñëa drew up the fine chariot in the midst of the armies of both parties.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: bhéñma-droëa-pramukhataù sarveñäà ca mahé-kñitäm uväca pärtha paçyaitän samavetän kurün iti
transliteration: bhenma-droea-pramukhatau sarvenaa ca mahe-knitam uvaca partha pacyaitan samavetan kurun iti
translation: In the presence of Bhéñma, Droëa and all other chieftains of the world, Håñékeça, the Lord, said, Just behold, Pärtha, all the Kurus who are assembled here.

glossary.gloss: all the members of the Kuru dynasty

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: taträpaçyat sthitän pärthaù pitèn atha pitämahän äcäryän mätulän bhrätèn puträn pauträn sakhéàs tathä çvaçurän suhådaç caiva senayor ubhayor api
transliteration: tatrapacyat sthitan parthau piten atha pitamahan acaryan matulan bhraten putran pautran sakheas tatha cvacuran suhadac caiva senayor ubhayor api
translation: There Arjuna could see, within the midst of the armies of both parties, his fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends, and also his father-in-law and well-wishers—all present there.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: tän samékñya sa kaunteyaù sarvän bandhün avasthitän kåpayä parayäviñöo viñédann idam abravét
transliteration: tan sameknya sa kaunteyau sarvan bandhun avasthitan kapaya parayavinoo vinedann idam abravet
translation: When the son of Kunté, Arjuna, saw all these different grades of friends and relatives, he became overwhelmed with compassion and spoke thus:
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: arjuna uväca dåñövemaà sva-janaà kåñëa yuyutsuà samupasthitam sédanti mama gäträëi mukhaà ca pariçuñyati
transliteration: arjuna uvaca danovemaa sva-janaa kanea yuyutsua samupasthitam sedanti mama gatraei mukhaa ca paricunyati
translation: Arjuna said: My dear Kåñëa, seeing my friends and relatives present before me in such a fighting spirit, I feel the limbs of my body quivering and my mouth drying up.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: vepathuç ca çarére me roma-harñaç ca jäyate gäëòévaà sraàsate hastät tvak caiva paridahyate
transliteration: vepathuc ca carere me roma-harnac ca jayate gaeoevaa sraasate hastat tvak caiva paridahyate
translation: My whole body is trembling, and my hair is standing on end. My bow Gäëòéva is slipping from my hand, and my skin is burning.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: na ca çaknomy avasthätuà bhramatéva ca me manaù nimittäni ca paçyämi viparétäni keçava
transliteration: na ca caknomy avasthatua bhramateva ca me manau nimittani ca pacyami viparetani kecava
translation: I am now unable to stand here any longer. I am forgetting myself, and my mind is reeling. I foresee only evil, O killer of the Keçé demon.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: na ca çreyo ’nupaçyämi hatvä sva-janam ähave na käìkñe vijayaà kåñëa na ca räjyaà sukhäni ca
transliteration: na ca creyo 'nupacyami hatva sva-janam ahave na kaikne vijayaa kanea na ca rajyaa sukhani ca
translation: I do not see how any good can come from killing my own kinsmen in this battle, nor can I, my dear Kåñëa, desire any subsequent victory, kingdom, or happiness.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: kià no räjyena govinda kià bhogair jévitena vä yeñäm arthe käìkñitaà no räjyaà bhogäù sukhäni ca
transliteration: kia no rajyena govinda kia bhogair jevitena va yenam arthe kaiknitaa no rajyaa bhogau sukhani ca
translation: O Govinda, of what avail to us are kingdoms, happiness or even life itself when all those for whom we may desire them are now arrayed in this battlefield? O Madhusüdana, when teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and all relatives are ready to give up their lives and properties and are standing before me, then why should I wish to kill them, though I may survive? O maintainer of all creatures, I am not prepared to fight with them even in exchange for the three worlds, let alone this earth.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: ta ime ’vasthitä yuddhe präëäàs tyaktvä dhanäni ca äcäryäù pitaraù puträs tathaiva ca pitämahäù
transliteration: ta ime 'vasthita yuddhe praeaas tyaktva dhanani ca acaryau pitarau putras tathaiva ca pitamahau
translation: O Govinda, of what avail to us are kingdoms, happiness or even life itself when all those for whom we may desire them are now arrayed in this battlefield? O Madhusüdana, when teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and all relatives are ready to give up their lives and properties and are standing before me, then why should I wish to kill them, though I may survive? O maintainer of all creatures, I am not prepared to fight with them even in exchange for the three worlds, let alone this earth.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: mätuläù çvaçuräù pauträù çyäläù sambandhinas tathä etän na hantum icchämi ghnato ’pi madhusüdana
transliteration: matulau cvacurau pautrau cyalau sambandhinas tatha etan na hantum icchami ghnato 'pi madhusudana
translation: O Govinda, of what avail to us are kingdoms, happiness or even life itself when all those for whom we may desire them are now arrayed in this battlefield? O Madhusüdana, when teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and all relatives are ready to give up their lives and properties and are standing before me, then why should I wish to kill them, though I may survive? O maintainer of all creatures, I am not prepared to fight with them even in exchange for the three worlds, let alone this earth.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: api trailokya-räjyasya hetoù kià nu mahé-kåte nihatya dhärtaräñörän naù kä prétiù syäj janärdana
transliteration: api trailokya-rajyasya hetou kia nu mahe-kate nihatya dhartaranoran nau ka pretiu syaj janardana
translation: O Govinda, of what avail to us are kingdoms, happiness or even life itself when all those for whom we may desire them are now arrayed in this battlefield? O Madhusüdana, when teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and all relatives are ready to give up their lives and properties and are standing before me, then why should I wish to kill them, though I may survive? O maintainer of all creatures, I am not prepared to fight with them even in exchange for the three worlds, let alone this earth.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: päpam eväçrayed asmän hatvaitän ätatäyinaù tasmän närhä vayaà hantuà dhärtaräñörän sa-bändhavän sva-janaà hi kathaà hatvä sukhinaù syäma mädhava
transliteration: papam evacrayed asman hatvaitan atatayinau tasman narha vayaa hantua dhartaranoran sa-bandhavan sva-janaa hi kathaa hatva sukhinau syama madhava
translation: Sin will overcome us if we slay such aggressors. Therefore it is not proper for us to kill the sons of Dhåtaräñöra and our friends. What should we gain, O Kåñëa, husband of the goddess of fortune, and how could we be happy by killing our own kinsmen?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: yady apy ete na paçyanti lobhopahata-cetasaù kula-kñaya-kåtaà doñaà mitra-drohe ca pätakam
transliteration: yady apy ete na pacyanti lobhopahata-cetasau kula-knaya-kataa donaa mitra-drohe ca patakam
translation: O Janärdana, although these men, overtaken by greed, see no fault in killing one’s family or quarreling with friends, why should we, with knowledge of the sin, engage in these acts?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: kathaà na jïeyam asmäbhiù päpäd asmän nivartitum kula-kñaya-kåtaà doñaà prapaçyadbhir janärdana
transliteration: kathaa na jieyam asmabhiu papad asman nivartitum kula-knaya-kataa donaa prapacyadbhir janardana
translation: O Janärdana, although these men, overtaken by greed, see no fault in killing one’s family or quarreling with friends, why should we, with knowledge of the sin, engage in these acts?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: kula-kñaye praëaçyanti kula-dharmäù sanätanäù dharme nañöe kulaà kåtsnam adharmo ’bhibhavaty uta
transliteration: kula-knaye praeacyanti kula-dharmau sanatanau dharme nanoe kulaa katsnam adharmo 'bhibhavaty uta
translation: With the destruction of dynasty, the eternal family tradition is vanquished, and thus the rest of the family becomes involved in irreligious practice.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: adharmäbhibhavät kåñëa praduñyanti kula-striyaù stréñu duñöäsu värñëeya jäyate varëa-saìkaraù
transliteration: adharmabhibhavat kanea pradunyanti kula-striyau strenu dunoasu varneeya jayate varea-saikarau
translation: When irreligion is prominent in the family, O Kåñëa, the women of the family become corrupt, and from the degradation of womanhood, O descendant of Våñëi, comes unwanted progeny.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: saìkaro narakäyaiva kula-ghnänäà kulasya ca patanti pitaro hy eñäà lupta-piëòodaka-kriyäù
transliteration: saikaro narakayaiva kula-ghnanaa kulasya ca patanti pitaro hy enaa lupta-pieoodaka-kriyau
translation: When there is increase of unwanted population, a hellish situation is created both for the family and for those who destroy the family tradition. In such corrupt families, there is no offering of oblations of food and water to the ancestors.

glossary.gloss: of those who are killers of the family

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: doñair etaiù kula-ghnänäà varëa-saìkara-kärakaiù utsädyante jäti-dharmäù kula-dharmäç ca çäçvatäù
transliteration: donair etaiu kula-ghnanaa varea-saikara-karakaiu utsadyante jati-dharmau kula-dharmac ca cacvatau
translation: Due to the evil deeds of the destroyers of family tradition, all kinds of community projects and family welfare activities are devastated.

glossary.gloss: of the destroyer of a family

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: utsanna-kula-dharmäëäà manuñyäëäà janärdana narake niyataà väso bhavatéty anuçuçruma
transliteration: utsanna-kula-dharmaeaa manunyaeaa janardana narake niyataa vaso bhavatety anucucruma
translation: O Kåñëa, maintainer of the people, I have heard by disciplic succession that those who destroy family traditions dwell always in hell.

glossary.gloss: of those who have the family traditions
I have heard by disciplic succession.

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: aho bata mahat päpaà kartuà vyavasitä vayam yad räjya-sukha-lobhena hantuà sva-janam udyatäù
transliteration: aho bata mahat papaa kartua vyavasita vayam yad rajya-sukha-lobhena hantua sva-janam udyatau
translation: Alas, how strange it is that we are preparing to commit greatly sinful acts, driven by the desire to enjoy royal happiness.

glossary.gloss: driven by greed for royal happiness

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: yadi mäm apratékäram açastraà çastra-päëayaù dhärtaräñörä raëe hanyus tan me kñemataraà bhavet
transliteration: yadi mam apratekaram acastraa castra-paeayau dhartaranora raee hanyus tan me knemataraa bhavet
translation: I would consider it better for the sons of Dhåtaräñöra to kill me unarmed and unresisting, rather than fight with them.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
iast: saïjaya uväca evam uktvärjunaù saìkhye rathopastha upäviçat visåjya sa-çaraà cäpaà çoka-saàvigna-mänasaù
transliteration: saijaya uvaca evam uktvarjunau saikhye rathopastha upavicat visajya sa-caraa capaa coka-saavigna-manasau
translation: Saïjaya said: Arjuna, having thus spoken on the battlefield, cast aside his bow and arrows and sat down on the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: saïjaya uväca taà tathä kåpayäviñöam açru-pürëäkulekñaëam viñédantam idaà väkyam uväca madhusüdanaù
transliteration: saijaya uvaca taa tatha kapayavinoam acru-pureakuleknaeam vinedantam idaa vakyam uvaca madhusudanau
translation: Saïjaya said: Seeing Arjuna full of compassion and very sorrowful, his eyes brimming with tears, Madhusüdana, Kåñëa, spoke the following words.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çré-bhagavän uväca kutas tvä kaçmalam idaà viñame samupasthitam anärya-juñöam asvargyam akérti-karam arjuna
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca kutas tva kacmalam idaa viname samupasthitam anarya-junoam asvargyam akerti-karam arjuna
translation: The Supreme Person [Bhagavän] said: My dear Arjuna, how have these impurities come upon you? They are not at all befitting a man who knows the progressive values of life. They do not lead to higher planets, but to infamy.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said
persons who do not know the value of life
that which does not lead to higher planets

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: klaibyaà mä sma gamaù pärtha naitat tvayy upapadyate kñudraà hådaya-daurbalyaà tyaktvottiñöha parantapa
transliteration: klaibyaa ma sma gamau partha naitat tvayy upapadyate knudraa hadaya-daurbalyaa tyaktvottinoha parantapa
translation: O son of Påthä, do not yield to this degrading impotence. It does not become you. Give up such petty weakness of heart and arise, O chastiser of the enemy.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: arjuna uväca kathaà bhéñmam ahaà saìkhye droëaà ca madhusüdana iñubhiù pratiyotsyämi püjärhäv ari-südana
transliteration: arjuna uvaca kathaa bhenmam ahaa saikhye droeaa ca madhusudana inubhiu pratiyotsyami pujarhav ari-sudana
translation: Arjuna said: O killer of Madhu [Kåñëa], how can I counterattack with arrows in battle men like Bhéñma and Droëa, who are worthy of my worship?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: gurün ahatvä hi mahänubhävän çreyo bhoktuà bhaikñyam apéha loke hatvärtha-kämäàs tu gurün ihaiva bhuïjéya bhogän rudhira-pradigdhän
transliteration: gurun ahatva hi mahanubhavan creyo bhoktua bhaiknyam apeha loke hatvartha-kamaas tu gurun ihaiva bhuijeya bhogan rudhira-pradigdhan
translation: It is better to live in this world by begging than to live at the cost of the lives of great souls who are my teachers. Even though they are avaricious, they are nonetheless superiors. If they are killed, our spoils will be tainted with blood.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: na caitad vidmaù kataran no garéyo yad vä jayema yadi vä no jayeyuù yän eva hatvä na jijéviñämas te ’vasthitäù pramukhe dhärtaräñöräù
transliteration: na caitad vidmau kataran no gareyo yad va jayema yadi va no jayeyuu yan eva hatva na jijevinamas te 'vasthitau pramukhe dhartaranorau
translation: Nor do we know which is better—conquering them or being conquered by them. The sons of Dhåtaräñöra, whom if we killed we should not care to live, are now standing before us on this battlefield.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: kärpaëya-doñopahata-svabhävaù påcchämi tväà dharma-sammüòha-cetäù yac chreyaù syän niçcitaà brühi tan me çiñyas te ’haà çädhi mäà tväà prapannam
transliteration: karpaeya-donopahata-svabhavau pacchami tvaa dharma-sammuoha-cetau yac chreyau syan niccitaa bruhi tan me cinyas te 'haa cadhi maa tvaa prapannam
translation: Now I am confused about my duty and have lost all composure because of weakness. In this condition I am asking You to tell me clearly what is best for me. Now I am Your disciple, and a soul surrendered unto You. Please instruct me.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: na hi prapaçyämi mamäpanudyäd yac chokam ucchoñaëam indriyäëäm aväpya bhümäv asapatnam åddhaà räjyaà suräëäm api cädhipatyam
transliteration: na hi prapacyami mamapanudyad yac chokam ucchonaeam indriyaeam avapya bhumav asapatnam addhaa rajyaa suraeam api cadhipatyam
translation: I can find no means to drive away this grief which is drying up my senses. I will not be able to destroy it even if I win an unrivalled kingdom on the earth with sovereignty like the demigods in heaven.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: saïjaya uväca evam uktvä håñékeçaà guòäkeçaù parantapaù na yotsya iti govindam uktvä tüñëéà babhüva ha
transliteration: saijaya uvaca evam uktva hanekecaa guoakecau parantapau na yotsya iti govindam uktva tuneea babhuva ha
translation: Saïjaya said: Having spoken thus, Arjuna, chastiser of enemies, told Kåñëa, “Govinda, I shall not fight,” and fell silent.

glossary.gloss: unto Kåñëa, the master of the senses
Arjuna, the master at curbing ignorance
unto Kåñëa, the giver of pleasure

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tam uväca håñékeçaù prahasann iva bhärata senayor ubhayor madhye viñédantam idaà vacaù
transliteration: tam uvaca hanekecau prahasann iva bharata senayor ubhayor madhye vinedantam idaa vacau
translation: O descendant of Bharata, at that time Kåñëa, smiling, in the midst of both the armies, spoke the following words to the grief-stricken Arjuna.

glossary.gloss: the master of the senses, Kåñëa

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çré-bhagavän uväca açocyän anvaçocas tvaà prajïä-vädäàç ca bhäñase gatäsün agatäsüàç ca nänuçocanti paëòitäù
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca acocyan anvacocas tvaa prajia-vadaac ca bhanase gatasun agatasuac ca nanucocanti paeoitau
translation: The Blessed Lord said: While speaking learned words, you are mourning for what is not worthy of grief. Those who are wise lament neither for the living nor the dead.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said
that which is not worthy of lamentation

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: na tv evähaà jätu näsaà na tvaà neme janädhipäù na caiva na bhaviñyämaù sarve vayam ataù param
transliteration: na tv evahaa jatu nasaa na tvaa neme janadhipau na caiva na bhavinyamau sarve vayam atau param
translation: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings; nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: dehino ’smin yathä dehe kaumäraà yauvanaà jarä tathä dehäntara-präptir dhéras tatra na muhyati
transliteration: dehino 'smin yatha dehe kaumaraa yauvanaa jara tatha dehantara-praptir dheras tatra na muhyati
translation: As the embodied soul continually passes, in this body, from boyhood to youth to old age, the soul similarly passes into another body at death. The self-realized soul is not bewildered by such a change.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: mäträ-sparçäs tu kaunteya çétoñëa-sukha-duùkha-däù ägamäpäyino ’nityäs täàs titikñasva bhärata
transliteration: matra-sparcas tu kaunteya cetonea-sukha-duukha-dau agamapayino 'nityas taas titiknasva bharata
translation: O son of Kunté, the nonpermanent appearance of happiness and distress, and their disappearance in due course, are like the appearance and disappearance of winter and summer seasons. They arise from sense perception, O scion of Bharata, and one must learn to tolerate them without being disturbed.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yaà hi na vyathayanty ete puruñaà puruñarñabha sama-duùkha-sukhaà dhéraà so ’måtatväya kalpate
transliteration: yaa hi na vyathayanty ete purunaa purunarnabha sama-duukha-sukhaa dheraa so 'matatvaya kalpate
translation: O best among men [Arjuna], the person who is not disturbed by happiness and distress and is steady in both is certainly eligible for liberation.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: näsato vidyate bhävo näbhävo vidyate sataù ubhayor api dåñöo ’ntas tv anayos tattva-darçibhiù
transliteration: nasato vidyate bhavo nabhavo vidyate satau ubhayor api danoo 'ntas tv anayos tattva-darcibhiu
translation: Those who are seers of the truth have concluded that of the nonexistent there is no endurance, and of the existent there is no cessation. This seers have concluded by studying the nature of both.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: avinäçi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaà tatam vinäçam avyayasyäsya na kaçcit kartum arhati
transliteration: avinaci tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaa tatam vinacam avyayasyasya na kaccit kartum arhati
translation: Know that which pervades the entire body is indestructible. No one is able to destroy the imperishable soul.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: antavanta ime dehä nityasyoktäù çarériëaù anäçino ’prameyasya tasmäd yudhyasva bhärata
transliteration: antavanta ime deha nityasyoktau carerieau anacino 'prameyasya tasmad yudhyasva bharata
translation: Only the material body of the indestructible, immeasurable and eternal living entity is subject to destruction; therefore, fight, O descendant of Bharata.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: ya enaà vetti hantäraà yaç cainaà manyate hatam ubhau tau na vijänéto näyaà hanti na hanyate
transliteration: ya enaa vetti hantaraa yac cainaa manyate hatam ubhau tau na vijaneto nayaa hanti na hanyate
translation: He who thinks that the living entity is the slayer or that he is slain, does not understand. One who is in knowledge knows that the self slays not nor is slain.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: na jäyate mriyate vä kadäcin näyaà bhütvä bhavitä vä na bhüyaù ajo nityaù çäçvato ’yaà puräëo na hanyate hanyamäne çarére
transliteration: na jayate mriyate va kadacin nayaa bhutva bhavita va na bhuyau ajo nityau cacvato 'yaa puraeo na hanyate hanyamane carere
translation: For the soul there is never birth nor death. Nor, having once been, does he ever cease to be. He is unborn, eternal, ever-existing, undying and primeval. He is not slain when the body is slain.

glossary.gloss: at any time (past, present or future)

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: vedävinäçinaà nityaà ya enam ajam avyayam kathaà sa puruñaù pärtha kaà ghätayati hanti kam
transliteration: vedavinacinaa nityaa ya enam ajam avyayam kathaa sa purunau partha kaa ghatayati hanti kam
translation: O Pärtha, how can a person who knows that the soul is indestructible, unborn, eternal and immutable, kill anyone or cause anyone to kill?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: väsäàsi jérëäni yathä vihäya naväni gåhëäti naro ’paräëi tathä çaréräëi vihäya jérëäny anyäni saàyäti naväni dehé
transliteration: vasaasi jereani yatha vihaya navani gaheati naro 'paraei tatha careraei vihaya jereany anyani saayati navani dehe
translation: As a person puts on new garments, giving up old ones, similarly, the soul accepts new material bodies, giving up the old and useless ones.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: nainaà chindanti çasträëi nainaà dahati pävakaù na cainaà kledayanty äpo na çoñayati märutaù
transliteration: nainaa chindanti castraei nainaa dahati pavakau na cainaa kledayanty apo na conayati marutau
translation: The soul can never be cut into pieces by any weapon, nor can he be burned by fire, nor moistened by water, nor withered by the wind.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: acchedyo ’yam adähyo ’yam akledyo ’çoñya eva ca nityaù sarva-gataù sthäëur acalo ’yaà sanätanaù
transliteration: acchedyo 'yam adahyo 'yam akledyo 'conya eva ca nityau sarva-gatau sthaeur acalo 'yaa sanatanau
translation: This individual soul is unbreakable and insoluble, and can be neither burned nor dried. He is everlasting, all-pervading, unchangeable, immovable and eternally the same.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: avyakto ’yam acintyo ’yam avikäryo ’yam ucyate tasmäd evaà viditvainaà nänuçocitum arhasi
transliteration: avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yam avikaryo 'yam ucyate tasmad evaa viditvainaa nanucocitum arhasi
translation: It is said that the soul is invisible, inconceivable, immutable, and unchangeable. Knowing this, you should not grieve for the body.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: atha cainaà nitya-jätaà nityaà vä manyase måtam tathäpi tvaà mahä-bäho nainaà çocitum arhasi
transliteration: atha cainaa nitya-jataa nityaa va manyase matam tathapi tvaa maha-baho nainaa cocitum arhasi
translation: If, however, you think that the soul is perpetually born and always dies, still you have no reason to lament, O mighty-armed.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: jätasya hi dhruvo måtyur dhruvaà janma måtasya ca tasmäd aparihärye ’rthe na tvaà çocitum arhasi
transliteration: jatasya hi dhruvo matyur dhruvaa janma matasya ca tasmad apariharye 'rthe na tvaa cocitum arhasi
translation: For one who has taken his birth, death is certain; and for one who is dead, birth is certain. Therefore, in the unavoidable discharge of your duty, you should not lament.

glossary.gloss: one who has taken his birth

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: avyaktädéni bhütäni vyakta-madhyäni bhärata avyakta-nidhanäny eva tatra kä paridevanä
transliteration: avyaktadeni bhutani vyakta-madhyani bharata avyakta-nidhanany eva tatra ka paridevana
translation: All created beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in their interim state, and unmanifest again when they are annihilated. So what need is there for lamentation?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: äçcarya-vat paçyati kaçcid enam äçcarya-vad vadati tathaiva cänyaù äçcarya-vac cainam anyaù çåëoti çrutväpy enaà veda na caiva kaçcit
transliteration: accarya-vat pacyati kaccid enam accarya-vad vadati tathaiva canyau accarya-vac cainam anyau caeoti crutvapy enaa veda na caiva kaccit
translation: Some look on the soul as amazing, some describe him as amazing, and some hear of him as amazing, while others, even after hearing about him, cannot understand him at all.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: dehé nityam avadhyo ’yaà dehe sarvasya bhärata tasmät sarväëi bhütäni na tvaà çocitum arhasi
transliteration: dehe nityam avadhyo 'yaa dehe sarvasya bharata tasmat sarvaei bhutani na tvaa cocitum arhasi
translation: O descendant of Bharata, he who dwells in the body is eternal and can never be slain. Therefore you need not grieve for any creature.

glossary.gloss: the owner of the material body

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: sva-dharmam api cävekñya na vikampitum arhasi dharmyäd dhi yuddhäc chreyo ’nyat kñatriyasya na vidyate
transliteration: sva-dharmam api caveknya na vikampitum arhasi dharmyad dhi yuddhac chreyo 'nyat knatriyasya na vidyate
translation: Considering your specific duty as a kñatriya, you should know that there is no better engagement for you than fighting on religious principles; and so there is no need for hesitation.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yadåcchayä copapannaà svarga-dväram apävåtam sukhinaù kñatriyäù pärtha labhante yuddham édåçam
transliteration: yadacchaya copapannaa svarga-dvaram apavatam sukhinau knatriyau partha labhante yuddham edacam
translation: O Pärtha, happy are the kñatriyas to whom such fighting opportunities come unsought, opening for them the doors of the heavenly planets.

glossary.gloss: the members of the royal order

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: atha cet tvam imaà dharmyaà saìgrämaà na kariñyasi tataù sva-dharmaà kértià ca hitvä päpam aväpsyasi
transliteration: atha cet tvam imaa dharmyaa saigramaa na karinyasi tatau sva-dharmaa kertia ca hitva papam avapsyasi
translation: If, however, you do not fight this religious war, then you will certainly incur sins for neglecting your duties and thus lose your reputation as a fighter.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: akértià cäpi bhütäni kathayiñyanti te ’vyayäm sambhävitasya cäkértir maraëäd atiricyate
transliteration: akertia capi bhutani kathayinyanti te 'vyayam sambhavitasya cakertir maraead atiricyate
translation: People will always speak of your infamy, and for one who has been honored, dishonor is worse than death.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: bhayäd raëäd uparataà maàsyante tväà mahä-rathäù yeñäà ca tvaà bahu-mato bhütvä yäsyasi läghavam
transliteration: bhayad raead uparataa maasyante tvaa maha-rathau yenaa ca tvaa bahu-mato bhutva yasyasi laghavam
translation: The great generals who have highly esteemed your name and fame will think that you have left the battlefield out of fear only, and thus they will consider you a coward.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: aväcya-vädäàç ca bahün vadiñyanti tavähitäù nindantas tava sämarthyaà tato duùkhataraà nu kim
transliteration: avacya-vadaac ca bahun vadinyanti tavahitau nindantas tava samarthyaa tato duukhataraa nu kim
translation: Your enemies will describe you in many unkind words and scorn your ability. What could be more painful for you?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: hato vä präpsyasi svargaà jitvä vä bhokñyase mahém tasmäd uttiñöha kaunteya yuddhäya kåta-niçcayaù
transliteration: hato va prapsyasi svargaa jitva va bhoknyase mahem tasmad uttinoha kaunteya yuddhaya kata-niccayau
translation: O son of Kunté, either you will be killed on the battlefield and attain the heavenly planets, or you will conquer and enjoy the earthly kingdom. Therefore get up and fight with determination.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: sukha-duùkhe same kåtvä läbhäläbhau jayäjayau tato yuddhäya yujyasva naivaà päpam aväpsyasi
transliteration: sukha-duukhe same katva labhalabhau jayajayau tato yuddhaya yujyasva naivaa papam avapsyasi
translation: Do thou fight for the sake of fighting, without considering happiness or distress, loss or gain, victory or defeat—and, by so doing, you shall never incur sin.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: eñä te ’bhihitä säìkhye buddhir yoge tv imäà çåëu buddhyä yukto yayä pärtha karma-bandhaà prahäsyasi
transliteration: ena te 'bhihita saikhye buddhir yoge tv imaa caeu buddhya yukto yaya partha karma-bandhaa prahasyasi
translation: Thus far I have declared to you the analytical knowledge of säìkhya philosophy. Now listen to the knowledge of yoga whereby one works without fruitive result. O son of Påthä, when you act by such intelligence, you can free yourself from the bondage of works.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: nehäbhikrama-näço ’sti pratyaväyo na vidyate sv-alpam apy asya dharmasya träyate mahato bhayät
transliteration: nehabhikrama-naco 'sti pratyavayo na vidyate sv-alpam apy asya dharmasya trayate mahato bhayat
translation: In this endeavor there is no loss or diminution, and a little advancement on this path can protect one from the most dangerous type of fear.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: vyavasäyätmikä buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana bahu-çäkhä hy anantäç ca buddhayo ’vyavasäyinäm
transliteration: vyavasayatmika buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana bahu-cakha hy anantac ca buddhayo 'vyavasayinam
translation: Those who are on this path are resolute in purpose, and their aim is one. O beloved child of the Kurus, the intelligence of those who are irresolute is manybranched.

glossary.gloss: O beloved child of the Kurus
of those who are not in Kåñëa consciousness.

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yäm imäà puñpitäà väcaà pravadanty avipaçcitaù veda-väda-ratäù pärtha nänyad astéti vädinaù
transliteration: yam imaa punpitaa vacaa pravadanty avipaccitau veda-vada-ratau partha nanyad asteti vadinau
translation: Men of small knowledge are very much attached to the flowery words of the Vedas, which recommend various fruitive activities for elevation to heavenly planets, resultant good birth, power, and so forth. Being desirous of sense gratification and opulent life, they say that there is nothing more than this.

glossary.gloss: men with a poor fund of knowledge

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: kämätmänaù svarga-parä janma-karma-phala-pradäm kriyä-viçeña-bahuläà bhogaiçvarya-gatià prati
transliteration: kamatmanau svarga-para janma-karma-phala-pradam kriya-vicena-bahulaa bhogaicvarya-gatia prati
translation: Men of small knowledge are very much attached to the flowery words of the Vedas, which recommend various fruitive activities for elevation to heavenly planets, resultant good birth, power, and so forth. Being desirous of sense gratification and opulent life, they say that there is nothing more than this.

glossary.gloss: men with a poor fund of knowledge

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: bhogaiçvarya-prasaktänäà tayäpahåta-cetasäm vyavasäyätmikä buddhiù samädhau na vidhéyate
transliteration: bhogaicvarya-prasaktanaa tayapahata-cetasam vyavasayatmika buddhiu samadhau na vidheyate
translation: In the minds of those who are too attached to sense enjoyment and material opulence, and who are bewildered by such things, the resolute determination of devotional service to the Supreme Lord does not take place.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: trai-guëya-viñayä vedä nistrai-guëyo bhavärjuna nirdvandvo nitya-sattva-stho niryoga-kñema ätmavän
transliteration: trai-gueya-vinaya veda nistrai-gueyo bhavarjuna nirdvandvo nitya-sattva-stho niryoga-knema atmavan
translation: The Vedas mainly deal with the subject of the three modes of material nature. Rise above these modes, O Arjuna. Be transcendental to all of them. Be free from all dualities and from all anxieties for gain and safety, and be established in the Self.

glossary.gloss: pertaining to the three modes of material nature
in a pure state of spiritual existence
free from the pains of opposites
free from (the thought of) acquisition and preservation

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yävän artha udapäne sarvataù samplutodake tävän sarveñu vedeñu brähmaëasya vijänataù
transliteration: yavan artha udapane sarvatau samplutodake tavan sarvenu vedenu brahmaeasya vijanatau
translation: All purposes that are served by the small pond can at once be served by the great reservoirs of water. Similarly, all the purposes of the Vedas can be served to one who knows the purpose behind them.

glossary.gloss: in a great reservoir of water
of the man who knows the Supreme Brahman
of one who is in complete knowledge.

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: karmaëy evädhikäras te mä phaleñu kadäcana mä karma-phala-hetur bhür mä te saìgo ’stv akarmaëi
transliteration: karmaey evadhikaras te ma phalenu kadacana ma karma-phala-hetur bhur ma te saigo 'stv akarmaei
translation: You have a right to perform your prescribed duty, but you are not entitled to the fruits of action. Never consider yourself to be the cause of the results of your activities, and never be attached to not doing your duty.

glossary.gloss: in the result of the work

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yoga-sthaù kuru karmäëi saìgaà tyaktvä dhanaïjaya siddhy-asiddhyoù samo bhütvä samatvaà yoga ucyate
transliteration: yoga-sthau kuru karmaei saigaa tyaktva dhanaijaya siddhy-asiddhyou samo bhutva samatvaa yoga ucyate
translation: Be steadfast in yoga, O Arjuna. Perform your duty and abandon all attachment to success or failure. Such evenness of mind is called yoga.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: düreëa hy avaraà karma buddhi-yogäd dhanaïjaya buddhau çaraëam anviccha kåpaëäù phala-hetavaù
transliteration: dureea hy avaraa karma buddhi-yogad dhanaijaya buddhau caraeam anviccha kapaeau phala-hetavau
translation: O Dhanaïjaya, rid yourself of all fruitive activities by devotional service, and surrender fully to that consciousness. Those who want to enjoy the fruits of their work are misers.

glossary.gloss: by discarding it at a long distance
on the strength of Kåñëa consciousness

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: buddhi-yukto jahätéha ubhe sukåta-duñkåte tasmäd yogäya yujyasva yogaù karmasu kauçalam
transliteration: buddhi-yukto jahateha ubhe sukata-dunkate tasmad yogaya yujyasva yogau karmasu kaucalam
translation: A man engaged in devotional service rids himself of both good and bad actions even in this life. Therefore strive for yoga, O Arjuna, which is the art of all work.

glossary.gloss: one who is engaged in devotional service
for the sake of devotional service

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: karma-jaà buddhi-yuktä hi phalaà tyaktvä manéñiëaù janma-bandha-vinirmuktäù padaà gacchanty anämayam
transliteration: karma-jaa buddhi-yukta hi phalaa tyaktva manenieau janma-bandha-vinirmuktau padaa gacchanty anamayam
translation: The wise, engaged in devotional service, take refuge in the Lord, and free themselves from the cycle of birth and death by renouncing the fruits of action in the material world. In this way they can attain that state beyond all miseries.

glossary.gloss: the bondage of birth and death

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yadä te moha-kalilaà buddhir vyatitariñyati tadä gantäsi nirvedaà çrotavyasya çrutasya ca
transliteration: yada te moha-kalilaa buddhir vyatitarinyati tada gantasi nirvedaa crotavyasya crutasya ca
translation: When your intelligence has passed out of the dense forest of delusion, you shall become indifferent to all that has been heard and all that is to be heard.

glossary.gloss: all that is to be heard

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çruti-vipratipannä te yadä sthäsyati niçcalä samädhäv acalä buddhis tadä yogam aväpsyasi
transliteration: cruti-vipratipanna te yada sthasyati niccala samadhav acala buddhis tada yogam avapsyasi
translation: When your mind is no longer disturbed by the flowery language of the Vedas, and when it remains fixed in the trance of self-realization, then you will have attained the Divine consciousness.

glossary.gloss: without being influenced by the fruitive results of the Vedas
in transcendental consciousness, or Kåñëa consciousness

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: arjuna uväca sthita-prajïasya kä bhäñä samädhi-sthasya keçava sthita-dhéù kià prabhäñeta kim äséta vrajeta kim
transliteration: arjuna uvaca sthita-prajiasya ka bhana samadhi-sthasya kecava sthita-dheu kia prabhaneta kim aseta vrajeta kim
translation: Arjuna said: What are the symptoms of one whose consciousness is thus merged in Transcendence? How does he speak, and what is his language? How does he sit, and how does he walk?

glossary.gloss: of one who is situated in fixed Kåñëa consciousness

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çré-bhagavän uväca prajahäti yadä kämän sarvän pärtha mano-gatän ätmany evätmanä tuñöaù sthita-prajïas tadocyate
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca prajahati yada kaman sarvan partha mano-gatan atmany evatmana tunoau sthita-prajias tadocyate
translation: The Blessed Lord said: O Pärtha, when a man gives up all varieties of sense desire which arise from mental concoction, and when his mind finds satisfaction in the self alone, then he is said to be in pure transcendental consciousness.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said
in the pure state of the soul

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: duùkheñv anudvigna-manäù sukheñu vigata-spåhaù véta-räga-bhaya-krodhaù sthita-dhér munir ucyate
transliteration: duukhenv anudvigna-manau sukhenu vigata-spahau veta-raga-bhaya-krodhau sthita-dher munir ucyate
translation: One who is not disturbed in spite of the threefold miseries, who is not elated when there is happiness, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady mind.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yaù sarvatränabhisnehas tat tat präpya çubhäçubham näbhinandati na dveñöi tasya prajïä pratiñöhitä
transliteration: yau sarvatranabhisnehas tat tat prapya cubhacubham nabhinandati na dvenoi tasya prajia pratinohita
translation: He who is without attachment, who does not rejoice when he obtains good, nor lament when he obtains evil, is firmly fixed in perfect knowledge.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yadä saàharate cäyaà kürmo ’ìgänéva sarvaçaù indriyäëéndriyärthebhyas tasya prajïä pratiñöhitä
transliteration: yada saaharate cayaa kurmo 'iganeva sarvacau indriyaeendriyarthebhyas tasya prajia pratinohita
translation: One who is able to withdraw his senses from sense objects, as the tortoise draws his limbs within the shell, is to be understood as truly situated in knowledge.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: viñayä vinivartante nirähärasya dehinaù rasa-varjaà raso ’py asya paraà dåñövä nivartate
transliteration: vinaya vinivartante niraharasya dehinau rasa-varjaa raso 'py asya paraa danova nivartate
translation: The embodied soul may be restricted from sense enjoyment, though the taste for sense objects remains. But, ceasing such engagements by experiencing a higher taste, he is fixed in consciousness.

glossary.gloss: are practiced to be refrained from

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yatato hy api kaunteya puruñasya vipaçcitaù indriyäëi pramäthéni haranti prasabhaà manaù
transliteration: yatato hy api kaunteya purunasya vipaccitau indriyaei pramatheni haranti prasabhaa manau
translation: The senses are so strong and impetuous, O Arjuna, that they forcibly carry away the mind even of a man of discrimination who is endeavoring to control them.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: täni sarväëi saàyamya yukta äséta mat-paraù vaçe hi yasyendriyäëi tasya prajïä pratiñöhitä
transliteration: tani sarvaei saayamya yukta aseta mat-parau vace hi yasyendriyaei tasya prajia pratinohita
translation: One who restrains his senses and fixes his consciousness upon Me is known as a man of steady intelligence.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: dhyäyato viñayän puàsaù saìgas teñüpajäyate saìgät saïjäyate kämaù kämät krodho ’bhijäyate
transliteration: dhyayato vinayan puasau saigas tenupajayate saigat saijayate kamau kamat krodho 'bhijayate
translation: While contemplating the objects of the senses, a person develops attachment for them, and from such attachment lust develops, and from lust anger arises.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: krodhäd bhavati sammohaù sammohät småti-vibhramaù småti-bhraàçäd buddhi-näço buddhi-näçät praëaçyati
transliteration: krodhad bhavati sammohau sammohat smati-vibhramau smati-bhraacad buddhi-naco buddhi-nacat praeacyati
translation: From anger, delusion arises, and from delusion bewilderment of memory. When memory is bewildered, intelligence is lost, and when intelligence is lost, one falls down again into the material pool.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: räga-dveña-vimuktais tu viñayän indriyaiç caran ätma-vaçyair vidheyätmä prasädam adhigacchati
transliteration: raga-dvena-vimuktais tu vinayan indriyaic caran atma-vacyair vidheyatma prasadam adhigacchati
translation: One who can control his senses by practicing the regulated principles of freedom can obtain the complete mercy of the Lord and thus become free from all attachment and aversion.

glossary.gloss: by one who has been free from such things

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: prasäde sarva-duùkhänäà hänir asyopajäyate prasanna-cetaso hy äçu buddhiù paryavatiñöhate
transliteration: prasade sarva-duukhanaa hanir asyopajayate prasanna-cetaso hy acu buddhiu paryavatinohate
translation: For one who is so situated in the Divine consciousness, the threefold miseries of material existence exist no longer; in such a happy state, one’s intelligence soon becomes steady.

glossary.gloss: on achievement of the causeless mercy of the Lord

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: nästi buddhir ayuktasya na cäyuktasya bhävanä na cäbhävayataù çäntir açäntasya kutaù sukham
transliteration: nasti buddhir ayuktasya na cayuktasya bhavana na cabhavayatau cantir acantasya kutau sukham
translation: One who is not in transcendental consciousness can have neither a controlled mind nor steady intelligence, without which there is no possibility of peace. And how can there be any happiness without peace?

glossary.gloss: of one who is not connected (with Kåñëa consciousness)
of one devoid of Kåñëa consciousness

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: indriyäëäà hi caratäà yan mano ’nuvidhéyate tad asya harati prajïäà väyur nävam ivämbhasi
transliteration: indriyaeaa hi carataa yan mano 'nuvidheyate tad asya harati prajiaa vayur navam ivambhasi
translation: As a boat on the water is swept away by a strong wind, even one of the senses on which the mind focuses can carry away a man’s intelligence.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tasmäd yasya mahä-bäho nigåhétäni sarvaçaù indriyäëéndriyärthebhyas tasya prajïä pratiñöhitä
transliteration: tasmad yasya maha-baho nigahetani sarvacau indriyaeendriyarthebhyas tasya prajia pratinohita
translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed, one whose senses are restrained from their objects is certainly of steady intelligence.

glossary.gloss: for the sake of sense objects

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yä niçä sarva-bhütänäà tasyäà jägarti saàyamé yasyäà jägrati bhütäni sä niçä paçyato muneù
transliteration: ya nica sarva-bhutanaa tasyaa jagarti saayame yasyaa jagrati bhutani sa nica pacyato muneu
translation: What is night for all beings is the time of awakening for the self-controlled; and the time of awakening for all beings is night for the introspective sage.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: äpüryamäëam acala-pratiñöhaà samudram äpaù praviçanti yadvat tadvat kämä yaà praviçanti sarve sa çäntim äpnoti na käma-kämé
transliteration: apuryamaeam acala-pratinohaa samudram apau pravicanti yadvat tadvat kama yaa pravicanti sarve sa cantim apnoti na kama-kame
translation: A person who is not disturbed by the incessant flow of desires—that enter like rivers into the ocean which is ever being filled but is always still—can alone achieve peace, and not the man who strives to satisfy such desires.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: vihäya kämän yaù sarvän pumäàç carati niùspåhaù nirmamo nirahaìkäraù sa çäntim adhigacchati
transliteration: vihaya kaman yau sarvan pumaac carati niuspahau nirmamo nirahaikarau sa cantim adhigacchati
translation: A person who has given up all desires for sense gratification, who lives free from desires, who has given up all sense of proprietorship and is devoid of false ego—he alone can attain real peace.

glossary.gloss: all material desires for sense gratification

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: eñä brähmé sthitiù pärtha nainäà präpya vimuhyati sthitväsyäm anta-käle ’pi brahma-nirväëam åcchati
transliteration: ena brahme sthitiu partha nainaa prapya vimuhyati sthitvasyam anta-kale 'pi brahma-nirvaeam acchati
translation: That is the way of the spiritual and godly life, after attaining which a man is not bewildered. Being so situated, even at the hour of death, one can enter into the kingdom of God.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: arjuna uväca jyäyasé cet karmaëas te matä buddhir janärdana tat kià karmaëi ghore mäà niyojayasi keçava
transliteration: arjuna uvaca jyayase cet karmaeas te mata buddhir janardana tat kia karmaei ghore maa niyojayasi kecava
translation: Arjuna said: O Janärdana, O Keçava, why do You urge me to engage in this ghastly warfare, if You think that intelligence is better than fruitive work?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: vyämiçreëeva väkyena buddhià mohayaséva me tad ekaà vada niçcitya yena çreyo ’ham äpnuyäm
transliteration: vyamicreeeva vakyena buddhia mohayaseva me tad ekaa vada niccitya yena creyo 'ham apnuyam
translation: My intelligence is bewildered by Your equivocal instructions. Therefore, please tell me decisively what is most beneficial for me.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çré-bhagavän uväca loke ’smin dvi-vidhä niñöhä purä proktä mayänagha jïäna-yogena säìkhyänäà karma-yogena yoginäm
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca loke 'smin dvi-vidha ninoha pura prokta mayanagha jiana-yogena saikhyanaa karma-yogena yoginam
translation: The Blessed Lord said: O sinless Arjuna, I have already explained that there are two classes of men who realize the Self. Some are inclined to understand Him by empirical, philosophical speculation, and others are inclined to know Him by devotional work.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said
by the linking process of knowledge
by the linking process of devotion

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: na karmaëäm anärambhän naiñkarmyaà puruño ’çnute na ca sannyasanäd eva siddhià samadhigacchati
transliteration: na karmaeam anarambhan nainkarmyaa puruno 'cnute na ca sannyasanad eva siddhia samadhigacchati
translation: Not by merely abstaining from work can one achieve freedom from reaction, nor by renunciation alone can one attain perfection.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: na hi kaçcit kñaëam api jätu tiñöhaty akarma-kåt käryate hy avaçaù karma sarvaù prakåti-jair guëaiù
transliteration: na hi kaccit knaeam api jatu tinohaty akarma-kat karyate hy avacau karma sarvau prakati-jair gueaiu
translation: All men are forced to act helplessly according to the impulses born of the modes of material nature; therefore no one can refrain from doing something, not even for a moment.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: karmendriyäëi saàyamya ya äste manasä smaran indriyärthän vimüòhätmä mithyäcäraù sa ucyate
transliteration: karmendriyaei saayamya ya aste manasa smaran indriyarthan vimuohatma mithyacarau sa ucyate
translation: One who restrains the senses and organs of action, but whose mind dwells on sense objects, certainly deludes himself and is called a pretender.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yas tv indriyäëi manasä niyamyärabhate ’rjuna karmendriyaiù karma-yogam asaktaù sa viçiñyate
transliteration: yas tv indriyaei manasa niyamyarabhate 'rjuna karmendriyaiu karma-yogam asaktau sa vicinyate
translation: On the other hand, he who controls the senses by the mind and engages his active organs in works of devotion, without attachment, is by far superior.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: niyataà kuru karma tvaà karma jyäyo hy akarmaëaù çaréra-yäträpi ca te na prasiddhyed akarmaëaù
transliteration: niyataa kuru karma tvaa karma jyayo hy akarmaeau carera-yatrapi ca te na prasiddhyed akarmaeau
translation: Perform your prescribed duty, for action is better than inaction. A man cannot even maintain his physical body without work.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yajïärthät karmaëo ’nyatra loko ’yaà karma-bandhanaù tad-arthaà karma kaunteya mukta-saìgaù samäcara
transliteration: yajiarthat karmaeo 'nyatra loko 'yaa karma-bandhanau tad-arthaa karma kaunteya mukta-saigau samacara
translation: Work done as a sacrifice for Viñëu has to be performed, otherwise work binds one to this material world. Therefore, O son of Kunté, perform your prescribed duties for His satisfaction, and in that way you will always remain unattached and free from bondage.

glossary.gloss: only for the sake of Yajïa, or Viñëu

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: saha-yajïäù prajäù såñövä puroväca prajäpatiù anena prasaviñyadhvam eña vo ’stv iñöa-käma-dhuk
transliteration: saha-yajiau prajau sanova purovaca prajapatiu anena prasavinyadhvam ena vo 'stv inoa-kama-dhuk
translation: In the beginning of creation, the Lord of all creatures sent forth generations of men and demigods, along with sacrifices for Viñëu, and blessed them by saying, “Be thou happy by this yajïa [sacrifice] because its performance will bestow upon you all desirable things.”
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: devän bhävayatänena te devä bhävayantu vaù parasparaà bhävayantaù çreyaù param aväpsyatha
transliteration: devan bhavayatanena te deva bhavayantu vau parasparaa bhavayantau creyau param avapsyatha
translation: The demigods, being pleased by sacrifices, will also please you; thus nourishing one another, there will reign general prosperity for all.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: iñöän bhogän hi vo devä däsyante yajïa-bhävitäù tair dattän apradäyaibhyo yo bhuìkte stena eva saù
transliteration: inoan bhogan hi vo deva dasyante yajia-bhavitau tair dattan apradayaibhyo yo bhuikte stena eva sau
translation: In charge of the various necessities of life, the demigods, being satisfied by the performance of yajïa [sacrifice], supply all necessities to man. But he who enjoys these gifts, without offering them to the demigods in return, is certainly a thief.

glossary.gloss: being satisfied by the performance of sacrifices

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yajïa-çiñöäçinaù santo mucyante sarva-kilbiñaiù bhuïjate te tv aghaà päpä ye pacanty ätma-käraëät
transliteration: yajia-cinoacinau santo mucyante sarva-kilbinaiu bhuijate te tv aghaa papa ye pacanty atma-karaeat
translation: The devotees of the Lord are released from all kinds of sins because they eat food which is offered first for sacrifice. Others, who prepare food for personal sense enjoyment, verily eat only sin.

glossary.gloss: food taken after performance of yajïa

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: annäd bhavanti bhütäni parjanyäd anna-sambhavaù yajïäd bhavati parjanyo yajïaù karma-samudbhavaù
transliteration: annad bhavanti bhutani parjanyad anna-sambhavau yajiad bhavati parjanyo yajiau karma-samudbhavau
translation: All living bodies subsist on food grains, which are produced from rain. Rains are produced by performance of yajïa [sacrifice], and yajïa is born of prescribed duties.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: karma brahmodbhavaà viddhi brahmäkñara-samudbhavam tasmät sarva-gataà brahma nityaà yajïe pratiñöhitam
transliteration: karma brahmodbhavaa viddhi brahmaknara-samudbhavam tasmat sarva-gataa brahma nityaa yajie pratinohitam
translation: Regulated activities are prescribed in the Vedas, and the Vedas are directly manifested from the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Consequently the allpervading Transcendence is eternally situated in acts of sacrifice.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: evaà pravartitaà cakraà nänuvartayatéha yaù aghäyur indriyärämo moghaà pärtha sa jévati
transliteration: evaa pravartitaa cakraa nanuvartayateha yau aghayur indriyaramo moghaa partha sa jevati
translation: My dear Arjuna, a man who does not follow this prescribed Vedic system of sacrifice certainly leads a life of sin, for a person delighting only in the senses lives in vain.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yas tv ätma-ratir eva syäd ätma-tåptaç ca mänavaù ätmany eva ca santuñöas tasya käryaà na vidyate
transliteration: yas tv atma-ratir eva syad atma-taptac ca manavau atmany eva ca santunoas tasya karyaa na vidyate
translation: One who is, however, taking pleasure in the self, who is illumined in the self, who rejoices in and is satisfied with the self only, fully satiated—for him there is no duty.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: naiva tasya kåtenärtho näkåteneha kaçcana na cäsya sarva-bhüteñu kaçcid artha-vyapäçrayaù
transliteration: naiva tasya katenartho nakateneha kaccana na casya sarva-bhutenu kaccid artha-vyapacrayau
translation: A self-realized man has no purpose to fulfill in the discharge of his prescribed duties, nor has he any reason not to perform such work. Nor has he any need to depend on any other living being.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tasmäd asaktaù satataà käryaà karma samäcara asakto hy äcaran karma param äpnoti püruñaù
transliteration: tasmad asaktau satataa karyaa karma samacara asakto hy acaran karma param apnoti purunau
translation: Therefore, without being attached to the fruits of activities, one should act as a matter of duty; for by working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: karmaëaiva hi saàsiddhim ästhitä janakädayaù loka-saìgraham eväpi sampaçyan kartum arhasi
transliteration: karmaeaiva hi saasiddhim asthita janakadayau loka-saigraham evapi sampacyan kartum arhasi
translation: Even kings like Janaka and others attained the perfectional stage by performance of prescribed duties. Therefore, just for the sake of educating the people in general, you should perform your work.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yad yad äcarati çreñöhas tat tad evetaro janaù sa yat pramäëaà kurute lokas tad anuvartate
transliteration: yad yad acarati crenohas tat tad evetaro janau sa yat pramaeaa kurute lokas tad anuvartate
translation: Whatever action is performed by a great man, common men follow in his footsteps. And whatever standards he sets by exemplary acts, all the world pursues.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: na me pärthästi kartavyaà triñu lokeñu kiïcana nänaväptam aväptavyaà varta eva ca karmaëi
transliteration: na me parthasti kartavyaa trinu lokenu kiicana nanavaptam avaptavyaa varta eva ca karmaei
translation: O son of Påthä, there is no work prescribed for Me within all the three planetary systems. Nor am I in want of anything, nor have I need to obtain anything—and yet I am engaged in work.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yadi hy ahaà na varteyaà jätu karmaëy atandritaù mama vartmänuvartante manuñyäù pärtha sarvaçaù
transliteration: yadi hy ahaa na varteyaa jatu karmaey atandritau mama vartmanuvartante manunyau partha sarvacau
translation: For, if I did not engage in work, O Pärtha, certainly all men would follow My path.

glossary.gloss: in the performance of prescribed duties

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: utsédeyur ime lokä na kuryäà karma ced aham saìkarasya ca kartä syäm upahanyäm imäù prajäù
transliteration: utsedeyur ime loka na kuryaa karma ced aham saikarasya ca karta syam upahanyam imau prajau
translation: If I should cease to work, then all these worlds would be put to ruination. I would also be the cause of creating unwanted population, and I would thereby destroy the peace of all sentient beings.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: saktäù karmaëy avidväàso yathä kurvanti bhärata kuryäd vidväàs tathäsaktaç cikérñur loka-saìgraham
transliteration: saktau karmaey avidvaaso yatha kurvanti bharata kuryad vidvaas tathasaktac cikernur loka-saigraham
translation: As the ignorant perform their duties with attachment to results, similarly the learned may also act, but without attachment, for the sake of leading people on the right path.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: na buddhi-bhedaà janayed ajïänäà karma-saìginäm joñayet sarva-karmäëi vidvän yuktaù samäcaran
transliteration: na buddhi-bhedaa janayed ajianaa karma-saiginam jonayet sarva-karmaei vidvan yuktau samacaran
translation: Let not the wise disrupt the minds of the ignorant who are attached to fruitive action. They should not be encouraged to refrain from work, but to engage in work in the spirit of devotion.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: prakåteù kriyamäëäni guëaiù karmäëi sarvaçaù ahaìkära-vimüòhätmä kartäham iti manyate
transliteration: prakateu kriyamaeani gueaiu karmaei sarvacau ahaikara-vimuohatma kartaham iti manyate
translation: The bewildered spirit soul, under the influence of the three modes of material nature, thinks himself to be the doer of activities, which are in actuality carried out by nature.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tattva-vit tu mahä-bäho guëa-karma-vibhägayoù guëä guëeñu vartanta iti matvä na sajjate
transliteration: tattva-vit tu maha-baho guea-karma-vibhagayou guea gueenu vartanta iti matva na sajjate
translation: One who is in knowledge of the Absolute Truth, O mighty-armed, does not engage himself in the senses and sense gratification, knowing well the differences between work in devotion and work for fruitive results.

glossary.gloss: the knower of the Absolute Truth

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: prakåter guëa-sammüòhäù sajjante guëa-karmasu tän akåtsna-vido mandän kåtsna-vin na vicälayet
transliteration: prakater guea-sammuohau sajjante guea-karmasu tan akatsna-vido mandan katsna-vin na vicalayet
translation: Bewildered by the modes of material nature, the ignorant fully engage themselves in material activities and become attached. But the wise should not unsettle them, although these duties are inferior due to the performers’ lack of knowledge.

glossary.gloss: persons with a poor fund of knowledge
one who is in factual knowledge

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: mayi sarväëi karmäëi sannyasyädhyätma-cetasä niräçér nirmamo bhütvä yudhyasva vigata-jvaraù
transliteration: mayi sarvaei karmaei sannyasyadhyatma-cetasa niracer nirmamo bhutva yudhyasva vigata-jvarau
translation: Therefore, O Arjuna, surrendering all your works unto Me, with mind intent on Me, and without desire for gain and free from egoism and lethargy, fight.

glossary.gloss: with full knowledge of the self

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: ye me matam idaà nityam anutiñöhanti mänaväù çraddhävanto ’nasüyanto mucyante te ’pi karmabhiù
transliteration: ye me matam idaa nityam anutinohanti manavau craddhavanto 'nasuyanto mucyante te 'pi karmabhiu
translation: One who executes his duties according to My injunctions and who follows this teaching faithfully, without envy, becomes free from the bondage of fruitive actions.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: ye tv etad abhyasüyanto nänutiñöhanti me matam sarva-jïäna-vimüòhäàs tän viddhi nañöän acetasaù
transliteration: ye tv etad abhyasuyanto nanutinohanti me matam sarva-jiana-vimuohaas tan viddhi nanoan acetasau
translation: But those who, out of envy, disregard these teachings and do not practice them regularly, are to be considered bereft of all knowledge, befooled, and doomed to ignorance and bondage.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: sadåçaà ceñöate svasyäù prakåter jïänavän api prakåtià yänti bhütäni nigrahaù kià kariñyati
transliteration: sadacaa cenoate svasyau prakater jianavan api prakatia yanti bhutani nigrahau kia karinyati
translation: Even a man of knowledge acts according to his own nature, for everyone follows his nature. What can repression accomplish?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: indriyasyendriyasyärthe räga-dveñau vyavasthitau tayor na vaçam ägacchet tau hy asya paripanthinau
transliteration: indriyasyendriyasyarthe raga-dvenau vyavasthitau tayor na vacam agacchet tau hy asya paripanthinau
translation: Attraction and repulsion for sense objects are felt by embodied beings, but one should not fall under the control of senses and sense objects because they are stumbling blocks on the path of self-realization.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çreyän sva-dharmo viguëaù para-dharmät sv-anuñöhität sva-dharme nidhanaà çreyaù para-dharmo bhayävahaù
transliteration: creyan sva-dharmo vigueau para-dharmat sv-anunohitat sva-dharme nidhanaa creyau para-dharmo bhayavahau
translation: It is far better to discharge one’s prescribed duties, even though they may be faulty, than another’s duties. Destruction in the course of performing one’s own duty is better than engaging in another’s duties, for to follow another’s path is dangerous.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: arjuna uväca atha kena prayukto ’yaà päpaà carati püruñaù anicchann api värñëeya baläd iva niyojitaù
transliteration: arjuna uvaca atha kena prayukto 'yaa papaa carati purunau anicchann api varneeya balad iva niyojitau
translation: Arjuna said: O descendant of Våñëi, by what is one impelled to sinful acts, even unwillingly, as if engaged by force?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çré-bhagavän uväca käma eña krodha eña rajo-guëa-samudbhavaù mahäçano mahä-päpmä viddhy enam iha vairiëam
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca kama ena krodha ena rajo-guea-samudbhavau mahacano maha-papma viddhy enam iha vairieam
translation: The Blessed Lord said: It is lust only, Arjuna, which is born of contact with the material modes of passion and later transformed into wrath, and which is the all-devouring, sinful enemy of this world.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: dhümenävriyate vahnir yathädarço malena ca yatholbenävåto garbhas tathä tenedam ävåtam
transliteration: dhumenavriyate vahnir yathadarco malena ca yatholbenavato garbhas tatha tenedam avatam
translation: As fire is covered by smoke, as a mirror is covered by dust, or as the embryo is covered by the womb, similarly, the living entity is covered by different degrees of this lust.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: ävåtaà jïänam etena jïänino nitya-vairiëä käma-rüpeëa kaunteya duñpüreëänalena ca
transliteration: avataa jianam etena jianino nitya-vairiea kama-rupeea kaunteya dunpureeanalena ca
translation: Thus, a man’s pure consciousness is covered by his eternal enemy in the form of lust, which is never satisfied and which burns like fire.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: indriyäëi mano buddhir asyädhiñöhänam ucyate etair vimohayaty eña jïänam ävåtya dehinam
transliteration: indriyaei mano buddhir asyadhinohanam ucyate etair vimohayaty ena jianam avatya dehinam
translation: The senses, the mind and the intelligence are the sitting places of this lust, which veils the real knowledge of the living entity and bewilders him.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tasmät tvam indriyäëy ädau niyamya bharatarñabha päpmänaà prajahi hy enaà jïäna-vijïäna-näçanam
transliteration: tasmat tvam indriyaey adau niyamya bharatarnabha papmanaa prajahi hy enaa jiana-vijiana-nacanam
translation: Therefore, O Arjuna, best of the Bhäratas, in the very beginning curb this great symbol of sin [lust] by regulating the senses, and slay this destroyer of knowledge and self-realization.

glossary.gloss: O chief amongst the descendants of Bharata
scientific knowledge of the pure soul

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: indriyäëi paräëy ähur indriyebhyaù paraà manaù manasas tu parä buddhir yo buddheù paratas tu saù
