transliteration: anapeknau cucir dakna udaseno gata-vyathau sarvarambha-parityage yo mad-bhaktau sa me priyau
translation: A devotee who is not dependant on the ordinary course of activities, who is pure, expert, without cares, free from all pains, and who does not strive for some result, is very dear to Me.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yo na håñyati na dveñöi na çocati na käìkñati çubhäçubha-parityägé bhaktimän yaù sa me priyaù
transliteration: yo na hanyati na dvenoi na cocati na kaiknati cubhacubha-parityage bhaktiman yau sa me priyau
translation: One who neither grasps pleasure or grief, who neither laments nor desires, and who renounces both auspicious and inauspicious things, is very dear to Me.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: samaù çatrau ca mitre ca tathä mänäpamänayoù çétoñëa-sukha-duùkheñu samaù saìga-vivarjitaù
transliteration: samau catrau ca mitre ca tatha manapamanayou cetonea-sukha-duukhenu samau saiga-vivarjitau
translation: One who is equal to friends and enemies, who is equiposed in honor and dishonor, heat and cold, happiness and distress, fame and infamy, who is always free from contamination, always silent and satisfied with anything, who doesn’t care for any residence, who is fixed in knowledge and engaged in devotional service, is very dear to Me.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tulya-nindä-stutir mauné santuñöo yena kenacit aniketaù sthira-matir bhaktimän me priyo naraù
transliteration: tulya-ninda-stutir maune santunoo yena kenacit aniketau sthira-matir bhaktiman me priyo narau
translation: One who is equal to friends and enemies, who is equiposed in honor and dishonor, heat and cold, happiness and distress, fame and infamy, who is always free from contamination, always silent and satisfied with anything, who doesn’t care for any residence, who is fixed in knowledge and engaged in devotional service, is very dear to Me.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: ye tu dharmämåtam idaà yathoktaà paryupäsate çraddadhänä mat-paramä bhaktäs te ’téva me priyäù
transliteration: ye tu dharmamatam idaa yathoktaa paryupasate craddadhana mat-parama bhaktas te 'teva me priyau
translation: He who follows this imperishable path of devotional service and who completely engages himself with faith, making Me the supreme goal, is very, very dear to Me.

glossary.gloss: taking the Supreme Lord as everything

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: arjuna uväca prakåtià puruñaà caiva kñetraà kñetra-jïam eva ca etad veditum icchämi jïänaà jïeyaà ca keçava
transliteration: arjuna uvaca prakatia purunaa caiva knetraa knetra-jiam eva ca etad veditum icchami jianaa jieyaa ca kecava
translation: Arjuna said: O my dear Kåñëa, I wish to know about prakåti [nature], Puruña [the enjoyer], and the field and the knower of the field, and of knowledge and the end of knowledge. The Blessed Lord then said: This body, O son of Kunté, is called the field, and one who knows this body is called the knower of the field.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çré-bhagavän uväca idaà çaréraà kaunteya kñetram ity abhidhéyate etad yo vetti taà prähuù kñetra-jïa iti tad-vidaù
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca idaa careraa kaunteya knetram ity abhidheyate etad yo vetti taa prahuu knetra-jia iti tad-vidau
translation: Arjuna said: O my dear Kåñëa, I wish to know about prakåti [nature], Puruña [the enjoyer], and the field and the knower of the field, and of knowledge and the end of knowledge. The Blessed Lord then said: This body, O son of Kunté, is called the field, and one who knows this body is called the knower of the field.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: kñetra-jïaà cäpi mäà viddhi sarva-kñetreñu bhärata kñetra-kñetrajïayor jïänaà yat taj jïänaà mataà mama
transliteration: knetra-jiaa capi maa viddhi sarva-knetrenu bharata knetra-knetrajiayor jianaa yat taj jianaa mataa mama
translation: O scion of Bharata, you should understand that I am also the knower in all bodies, and to understand this body and its owner is called knowledge. That is My opinion.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tat kñetraà yac ca yädåk ca yad-vikäri yataç ca yat sa ca yo yat-prabhävaç ca tat samäsena me çåëu
transliteration: tat knetraa yac ca yadak ca yad-vikari yatac ca yat sa ca yo yat-prabhavac ca tat samasena me caeu
translation: Now please hear My brief description of this field of activity and how it is constituted, what its changes are, whence it is produced, who that knower of the field of activities is, and what his influences are.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: åñibhir bahudhä gétaà chandobhir vividhaiù påthak brahma-sütra-padaiç caiva hetumadbhir viniçcitaiù
transliteration: anibhir bahudha getaa chandobhir vividhaiu pathak brahma-sutra-padaic caiva hetumadbhir viniccitaiu
translation: That knowledge of the field of activities and of the knower of activities is described by various sages in various Vedic writings—especially in the Vedänta-sütra—and is presented with all reasoning as to cause and effect.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: mahä-bhütäny ahaìkäro buddhir avyaktam eva ca indriyäëi daçaikaà ca païca cendriya-gocaräù
transliteration: maha-bhutany ahaikaro buddhir avyaktam eva ca indriyaei dacaikaa ca paica cendriya-gocarau
translation: The five great elements, false ego, intelligence, the unmanifested, the ten senses, the mind, the five sense objects, desire, hatred, happiness, distress, the aggregate, the life symptoms, and convictions—all these are considered, in summary, to be the field of activities and its interactions.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: icchä dveñaù sukhaà duùkhaà saìghätaç cetanä dhåtiù etat kñetraà samäsena sa-vikäram udähåtam
transliteration: iccha dvenau sukhaa duukhaa saighatac cetana dhatiu etat knetraa samasena sa-vikaram udahatam
translation: The five great elements, false ego, intelligence, the unmanifested, the ten senses, the mind, the five sense objects, desire, hatred, happiness, distress, the aggregate, the life symptoms, and convictions—all these are considered, in summary, to be the field of activities and its interactions.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: amänitvam adambhitvam ahiàsä kñäntir ärjavam äcäryopäsanaà çaucaà sthairyam ätma-vinigrahaù
transliteration: amanitvam adambhitvam ahiasa knantir arjavam acaryopasanaa caucaa sthairyam atma-vinigrahau
translation: Humility, pridelessness, nonviolence, tolerance, simplicity, approaching a bona fide spiritual master, cleanliness, steadiness and self-control; renunciation of the objects of sense gratification, absence of false ego, the perception of the evil of birth, death, old age and disease; nonattachment to children, wife, home and the rest, and evenmindedness amid pleasant and unpleasant events; constant and unalloyed devotion to Me, resorting to solitary places, detachment from the general mass of people; accepting the importance of self-realization, and philosophical search for the Absolute Truth—all these I thus declare to be knowledge, and what is contrary to these is ignorance.

glossary.gloss: approaching a bona fide spiritual master
in the matter of the senses

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: indriyärtheñu vairägyam anahaìkära eva ca janma-måtyu-jarä-vyädhiduùkha-doñänudarçanam asaktir anabhiñvaìgaù
transliteration: indriyarthenu vairagyam anahaikara eva ca janma-matyu-jara-vyadhiduukha-donanudarcanam asaktir anabhinvaigau
translation: Humility, pridelessness, nonviolence, tolerance, simplicity, approaching a bona fide spiritual master, cleanliness, steadiness and self-control; renunciation of the objects of sense gratification, absence of false ego, the perception of the evil of birth, death, old age and disease; nonattachment to children, wife, home and the rest, and evenmindedness amid pleasant and unpleasant events; constant and unalloyed devotion to Me, resorting to solitary places, detachment from the general mass of people; accepting the importance of self-realization, and philosophical search for the Absolute Truth—all these I thus declare to be knowledge, and what is contrary to these is ignorance.

glossary.gloss: approaching a bona fide spiritual master
in the matter of the senses

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: putra-dära-gåhädiñu nityaà ca sama-cittatvam iñöäniñöopapattiñu mayi cänanya-yogena
transliteration: putra-dara-gahadinu nityaa ca sama-cittatvam inoaninoopapattinu mayi cananya-yogena
translation: Humility, pridelessness, nonviolence, tolerance, simplicity, approaching a bona fide spiritual master, cleanliness, steadiness and self-control; renunciation of the objects of sense gratification, absence of false ego, the perception of the evil of birth, death, old age and disease; nonattachment to children, wife, home and the rest, and evenmindedness amid pleasant and unpleasant events; constant and unalloyed devotion to Me, resorting to solitary places, detachment from the general mass of people; accepting the importance of self-realization, and philosophical search for the Absolute Truth—all these I thus declare to be knowledge, and what is contrary to these is ignorance.

glossary.gloss: approaching a bona fide spiritual master
in the matter of the senses

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: bhaktir avyabhicäriëé vivikta-deça-sevitvam aratir jana-saàsadi adhyätma-jïäna-nityatvaà
transliteration: bhaktir avyabhicariee vivikta-deca-sevitvam aratir jana-saasadi adhyatma-jiana-nityatvaa
translation: Humility, pridelessness, nonviolence, tolerance, simplicity, approaching a bona fide spiritual master, cleanliness, steadiness and self-control; renunciation of the objects of sense gratification, absence of false ego, the perception of the evil of birth, death, old age and disease; nonattachment to children, wife, home and the rest, and evenmindedness amid pleasant and unpleasant events; constant and unalloyed devotion to Me, resorting to solitary places, detachment from the general mass of people; accepting the importance of self-realization, and philosophical search for the Absolute Truth—all these I thus declare to be knowledge, and what is contrary to these is ignorance.

glossary.gloss: approaching a bona fide spiritual master
in the matter of the senses

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tattva-jïänärtha-darçanam etaj jïänam iti proktam ajïänaà yad ato ’nyathä
transliteration: tattva-jianartha-darcanam etaj jianam iti proktam ajianaa yad ato 'nyatha
translation: Humility, pridelessness, nonviolence, tolerance, simplicity, approaching a bona fide spiritual master, cleanliness, steadiness and self-control; renunciation of the objects of sense gratification, absence of false ego, the perception of the evil of birth, death, old age and disease; nonattachment to children, wife, home and the rest, and evenmindedness amid pleasant and unpleasant events; constant and unalloyed devotion to Me, resorting to solitary places, detachment from the general mass of people; accepting the importance of self-realization, and philosophical search for the Absolute Truth—all these I thus declare to be knowledge, and what is contrary to these is ignorance.

glossary.gloss: approaching a bona fide spiritual master
in the matter of the senses

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: jïeyaà yat tat pravakñyämi yaj jïätvämåtam açnute anädi mat-paraà brahma na sat tan näsad ucyate
transliteration: jieyaa yat tat pravaknyami yaj jiatvamatam acnute anadi mat-paraa brahma na sat tan nasad ucyate
translation: I shall now explain the knowable, knowing which you will taste the eternal. This is beginningless, and it is subordinate to Me. It is called Brahman, the spirit, and it lies beyond the cause and effect of this material world.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: sarvataù päëi-pädaà tat sarvato ’kñi-çiro-mukham sarvataù çrutimal loke sarvam ävåtya tiñöhati
transliteration: sarvatau paei-padaa tat sarvato 'kni-ciro-mukham sarvatau crutimal loke sarvam avatya tinohati
translation: Everywhere are His hands and legs, His eyes and faces, and He hears everything. In this way the Supersoul exists.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: sarvendriya-guëäbhäsaà sarvendriya-vivarjitam asaktaà sarva-bhåc caiva nirguëaà guëa-bhoktå ca
transliteration: sarvendriya-gueabhasaa sarvendriya-vivarjitam asaktaa sarva-bhac caiva nirgueaa guea-bhokta ca
translation: The Supersoul is the original source of all senses, yet He is without senses. He is unattached, although He is the maintainer of all living beings. He transcends the modes of nature, and at the same time He is the master of all modes of material nature.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: bahir antaç ca bhütänäm acaraà caram eva ca sükñmatvät tad avijïeyaà düra-sthaà cäntike ca tat
transliteration: bahir antac ca bhutanam acaraa caram eva ca suknmatvat tad avijieyaa dura-sthaa cantike ca tat
translation: The Supreme Truth exists both internally and externally, in the moving and nonmoving. He is beyond the power of the material senses to see or to know. Although far, far away, He is also near to all.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: avibhaktaà ca bhüteñu vibhaktam iva ca sthitam bhüta-bhartå ca taj jïeyaà grasiñëu prabhaviñëu ca
transliteration: avibhaktaa ca bhutenu vibhaktam iva ca sthitam bhuta-bharta ca taj jieyaa grasineu prabhavineu ca
translation: Although the Supersoul appears to be divided, He is never divided. He is situated as one. Although He is the maintainer of every living entity, it is to be understood that He devours and develops all.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: jyotiñäm api taj jyotis tamasaù param ucyate jïänaà jïeyaà jïäna-gamyaà hådi sarvasya viñöhitam
transliteration: jyotinam api taj jyotis tamasau param ucyate jianaa jieyaa jiana-gamyaa hadi sarvasya vinohitam
translation: He is the source of light in all luminous objects. He is beyond the darkness of matter and is unmanifested. He is knowledge, He is the object of knowledge, and He is the goal of knowledge. He is situated in everyone’s heart.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: iti kñetraà tathä jïänaà jïeyaà coktaà samäsataù mad-bhakta etad vijïäya mad-bhäväyopapadyate
transliteration: iti knetraa tatha jianaa jieyaa coktaa samasatau mad-bhakta etad vijiaya mad-bhavayopapadyate
translation: Thus the field of activities [the body], knowledge, and the knowable have been summarily described by Me. Only My devotees can understand this thoroughly and thus attain to My nature.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: prakåtià puruñaà caiva viddhy anädé ubhäv api vikäräàç ca guëäàç caiva viddhi prakåti-sambhavän
transliteration: prakatia purunaa caiva viddhy anade ubhav api vikaraac ca gueaac caiva viddhi prakati-sambhavan
translation: Material nature and the living entities should be understood to be beginningless. Their transformations and the modes of matter are products of material nature.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: kärya-käraëa-kartåtve hetuù prakåtir ucyate puruñaù sukha-duùkhänäà bhoktåtve hetur ucyate
transliteration: karya-karaea-kartatve hetuu prakatir ucyate purunau sukha-duukhanaa bhoktatve hetur ucyate
translation: Nature is said to be the cause of all material activities and effects, whereas the living entity is the cause of the various sufferings and enjoyments in this world.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: puruñaù prakåti-stho hi bhuìkte prakåti-jän guëän käraëaà guëa-saìgo ’sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu
transliteration: purunau prakati-stho hi bhuikte prakati-jan guean karaeaa guea-saigo 'sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu
translation: The living entity in material nature thus follows the ways of life, enjoying the three modes of nature. This is due to his association with that material nature. Thus he meets with good and evil amongst various species.

glossary.gloss: being situated in the material energy
association with the modes of nature

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: upadrañöänumantä ca bhartä bhoktä maheçvaraù paramätmeti cäpy ukto dehe ’smin puruñaù paraù
transliteration: upadranoanumanta ca bharta bhokta mahecvarau paramatmeti capy ukto dehe 'smin purunau parau
translation: Yet in this body there is another, a transcendental enjoyer who is the Lord, the supreme proprietor, who exists as the overseer and permitter, and who is known as the Supersoul.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: ya evaà vetti puruñaà prakåtià ca guëaiù saha sarvathä vartamäno ’pi na sa bhüyo ’bhijäyate
transliteration: ya evaa vetti purunaa prakatia ca gueaiu saha sarvatha vartamano 'pi na sa bhuyo 'bhijayate
translation: One who understands this philosophy concerning material nature, the living entity and the interaction of the modes of nature is sure to attain liberation. He will not take birth here again, regardless of his present position.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: dhyänenätmani paçyanti kecid ätmänam ätmanä anye säìkhyena yogena karma-yogena cäpare
transliteration: dhyanenatmani pacyanti kecid atmanam atmana anye saikhyena yogena karma-yogena capare
translation: That Supersoul is perceived by some through meditation, by some through the cultivation of knowledge, and by others through working without fruitive desire.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: anye tv evam ajänantaù çrutvänyebhya upäsate te ’pi cätitaranty eva måtyuà çruti-paräyaëäù
transliteration: anye tv evam ajanantau crutvanyebhya upasate te 'pi catitaranty eva matyua cruti-parayaeau
translation: Again there are those who, although not conversant in spiritual knowledge, begin to worship the Supreme Person upon hearing about Him from others. Because of their tendency to hear from authorities, they also transcend the path of birth and death.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yävat saïjäyate kiïcit sattvaà sthävara-jaìgamam kñetra-kñetrajïa-saàyogät tad viddhi bharatarñabha
transliteration: yavat saijayate kiicit sattvaa sthavara-jaigamam knetra-knetrajia-saayogat tad viddhi bharatarnabha
translation: O chief of the Bhäratas, whatever you see in existence, both moving and unmoving, is only the combination of the field of activities and the knower of the field.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: samaà sarveñu bhüteñu tiñöhantaà parameçvaram vinaçyatsv avinaçyantaà yaù paçyati sa paçyati
transliteration: samaa sarvenu bhutenu tinohantaa paramecvaram vinacyatsv avinacyantaa yau pacyati sa pacyati
translation: One who sees the Supersoul accompanying the individual soul in all bodies and who understands that neither the soul nor the Supersoul is ever destroyed, actually sees.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: samaà paçyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam éçvaram na hinasty ätmanätmänaà tato yäti paräà gatim
transliteration: samaa pacyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam ecvaram na hinasty atmanatmanaa tato yati paraa gatim
translation: One who sees the Supersoul in every living being and equal everywhere does not degrade himself by his mind. Thus he approaches the transcendental destination.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: prakåtyaiva ca karmäëi kriyamäëäni sarvaçaù yaù paçyati tathätmänam akartäraà sa paçyati
transliteration: prakatyaiva ca karmaei kriyamaeani sarvacau yau pacyati tathatmanam akartaraa sa pacyati
translation: One who can see that all activities are performed by the body, which is created of material nature, and sees that the self does nothing, actually sees.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yadä bhüta-påthag-bhävam eka-stham anupaçyati tata eva ca vistäraà brahma sampadyate tadä
transliteration: yada bhuta-pathag-bhavam eka-stham anupacyati tata eva ca vistaraa brahma sampadyate tada
translation: When a sensible man ceases to see different identities, which are due to different material bodies, he attains to the Brahman conception. Thus he sees that beings are expanded everywhere.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: anäditvän nirguëatvät paramätmäyam avyayaù çaréra-stho ’pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate
transliteration: anaditvan nirgueatvat paramatmayam avyayau carera-stho 'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate
translation: Those with the vision of eternity can see that the soul is transcendental, eternal, and beyond the modes of nature. Despite contact with the material body, O Arjuna, the soul neither does anything nor is entangled.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yathä sarva-gataà saukñmyäd äkäçaà nopalipyate sarvaträvasthito dehe tathätmä nopalipyate
transliteration: yatha sarva-gataa sauknmyad akacaa nopalipyate sarvatravasthito dehe tathatma nopalipyate
translation: The sky, due to its subtle nature, does not mix with anything, although it is allpervading. Similarly, the soul, situated in Brahman vision, does not mix with the body, though situated in that body.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yathä prakäçayaty ekaù kåtsnaà lokam imaà raviù kñetraà kñetré tathä kåtsnaà prakäçayati bhärata
transliteration: yatha prakacayaty ekau katsnaa lokam imaa raviu knetraa knetre tatha katsnaa prakacayati bharata
translation: O son of Bharata, as the sun alone illuminates all this universe, so does the living entity, one within the body, illuminate the entire body by consciousness.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: kñetra-kñetrajïayor evam antaraà jïäna-cakñuñä bhüta-prakåti-mokñaà ca ye vidur yänti te param
transliteration: knetra-knetrajiayor evam antaraa jiana-caknuna bhuta-prakati-moknaa ca ye vidur yanti te param
translation: One who knowingly sees this difference between the body and the owner of the body and can understand the process of liberation from this bondage, also attains to the supreme goal.

glossary.gloss: of the proprietor of the body

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: çré-bhagavän uväca paraà bhüyaù pravakñyämi jïänänäà jïänam uttamam yaj jïätvä munayaù sarve paräà siddhim ito gatäù
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca paraa bhuyau pravaknyami jiananaa jianam uttamam yaj jiatva munayau sarve paraa siddhim ito gatau
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Again I shall declare to you this supreme wisdom, the best of all knowledge, knowing which all the sages have attained to supreme perfection.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: idaà jïänam upäçritya mama sädharmyam ägatäù sarge ’pi nopajäyante pralaye na vyathanti ca
transliteration: idaa jianam upacritya mama sadharmyam agatau sarge 'pi nopajayante pralaye na vyathanti ca
translation: By becoming fixed in this knowledge, one can attain to the transcendental nature, which is like My own nature. Thus established, one is not born at the time of creation nor disturbed at the time of dissolution.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbhaà dadhämy aham sambhavaù sarva-bhütänäà tato bhavati bhärata
transliteration: mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbhaa dadhamy aham sambhavau sarva-bhutanaa tato bhavati bharata
translation: The total material substance, called Brahman, is the source of birth, and it is that Brahman that I impregnate, making possible the births of all living beings, O son of Bharata.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: sarva-yoniñu kaunteya mürtayaù sambhavanti yäù täsäà brahma mahad yonir ahaà béja-pradaù pitä
transliteration: sarva-yoninu kaunteya murtayau sambhavanti yau tasaa brahma mahad yonir ahaa beja-pradau pita
translation: It should be understood that all species of life, O son of Kunté, are made possible by birth in this material nature, and that I am the seed-giving father.

glossary.gloss: the source of birth in the material substance

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: sattvaà rajas tama iti guëäù prakåti-sambhaväù nibadhnanti mahä-bäho dehe dehinam avyayam
transliteration: sattvaa rajas tama iti gueau prakati-sambhavau nibadhnanti maha-baho dehe dehinam avyayam
translation: Material nature consists of the three modes—goodness, passion and ignorance. When the living entity comes in contact with nature, he becomes conditioned by these modes.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: tatra sattvaà nirmalatvät prakäçakam anämayam sukha-saìgena badhnäti jïäna-saìgena cänagha
transliteration: tatra sattvaa nirmalatvat prakacakam anamayam sukha-saigena badhnati jiana-saigena canagha
translation: O sinless one, the mode of goodness, being purer than the others, is illuminating, and it frees one from all sinful reactions. Those situated in that mode develop knowledge, but they become conditioned by the concept of happiness.

glossary.gloss: being purest in the material world

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: rajo rägätmakaà viddhi tåñëä-saìga-samudbhavam tan nibadhnäti kaunteya karma-saìgena dehinam
transliteration: rajo ragatmakaa viddhi tanea-saiga-samudbhavam tan nibadhnati kaunteya karma-saigena dehinam
translation: The mode of passion is born of unlimited desires and longings, O son of Kunté, and because of this one is bound to material fruitive activities.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: tamas tv ajïäna-jaà viddhi mohanaà sarva-dehinäm pramädälasya-nidräbhis tan nibadhnäti bhärata
transliteration: tamas tv ajiana-jaa viddhi mohanaa sarva-dehinam pramadalasya-nidrabhis tan nibadhnati bharata
translation: O son of Bharata, the mode of ignorance causes the delusion of all living entities. The result of this mode is madness, indolence and sleep, which bind the conditioned soul.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: sattvaà sukhe saïjayati rajaù karmaëi bhärata jïänam ävåtya tu tamaù pramäde saïjayaty uta
transliteration: sattvaa sukhe saijayati rajau karmaei bharata jianam avatya tu tamau pramade saijayaty uta
translation: The mode of goodness conditions one to happiness, passion conditions him to the fruits of action, and ignorance to madness.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: rajas tamaç cäbhibhüya sattvaà bhavati bhärata rajaù sattvaà tamaç caiva tamaù sattvaà rajas tathä
transliteration: rajas tamac cabhibhuya sattvaa bhavati bharata rajau sattvaa tamac caiva tamau sattvaa rajas tatha
translation: Sometimes the mode of passion becomes prominent, defeating the mode of goodness, O son of Bharata. And sometimes the mode of goodness defeats passion, and at other times the mode of ignorance defeats goodness and passion. In this way there is always competition for supremacy.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: sarva-dväreñu dehe ’smin prakäça upajäyate jïänaà yadä tadä vidyäd vivåddhaà sattvam ity uta
transliteration: sarva-dvarenu dehe 'smin prakaca upajayate jianaa yada tada vidyad vivaddhaa sattvam ity uta
translation: The manifestations of the mode of goodness can be experienced when all the gates of the body are illuminated by knowledge.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: lobhaù pravåttir ärambhaù karmaëäm açamaù spåhä rajasy etäni jäyante vivåddhe bharatarñabha
transliteration: lobhau pravattir arambhau karmaeam acamau spaha rajasy etani jayante vivaddhe bharatarnabha
translation: O chief of the Bhäratas, when there is an increase in the mode of passion, the symptoms of great attachment, uncontrollable desire, hankering, and intense endeavor develop.

glossary.gloss: O chief of the descendants of Bharata.

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: aprakäço ’pravåttiç ca pramädo moha eva ca tamasy etäni jäyante vivåddhe kuru-nandana
transliteration: aprakaco 'pravattic ca pramado moha eva ca tamasy etani jayante vivaddhe kuru-nandana
translation: O son of Kuru, when there is an increase in the mode of ignorance madness, illusion, inertia and darkness are manifested.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: yadä sattve pravåddhe tu pralayaà yäti deha-bhåt tadottama-vidäà lokän amalän pratipadyate
transliteration: yada sattve pravaddhe tu pralayaa yati deha-bhat tadottama-vidaa lokan amalan pratipadyate
translation: When one dies in the mode of goodness, he attains to the pure higher planets.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: rajasi pralayaà gatvä karma-saìgiñu jäyate tathä pralénas tamasi müòha-yoniñu jäyate
transliteration: rajasi pralayaa gatva karma-saiginu jayate tatha pralenas tamasi muoha-yoninu jayate
translation: When one dies in the mode of passion, he takes birth among those engaged in fruitive activities; and when he dies in the mode of ignorance, he takes birth in the animal kingdom.

glossary.gloss: in the association of fruitive activities

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: karmaëaù sukåtasyähuù sättvikaà nirmalaà phalam rajasas tu phalaà duùkham ajïänaà tamasaù phalam
transliteration: karmaeau sukatasyahuu sattvikaa nirmalaa phalam rajasas tu phalaa duukham ajianaa tamasau phalam
translation: By acting in the mode of goodness, one becomes purified. Works done in the mode of passion result in distress, and actions performed in the mode of ignorance result in foolishness.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: sattvät saïjäyate jïänaà rajaso lobha eva ca pramäda-mohau tamaso bhavato ’jïänam eva ca
transliteration: sattvat saijayate jianaa rajaso lobha eva ca pramada-mohau tamaso bhavato 'jianam eva ca
translation: From the mode of goodness, real knowledge develops; from the mode of passion, grief develops; and from the mode of ignorance, foolishness, madness and illusion develop.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: ürdhvaà gacchanti sattva-sthä madhye tiñöhanti räjasäù jaghanya-guëa-våtti-sthä adho gacchanti tämasäù
transliteration: urdhvaa gacchanti sattva-stha madhye tinohanti rajasau jaghanya-guea-vatti-stha adho gacchanti tamasau
translation: Those situated in the mode of goodness gradually go upward to the higher planets; those in the mode of passion live on the earthly planets; and those in the mode of ignorance go down to the hellish worlds.

glossary.gloss: one who is situated in the mode of goodness
those who are situated in the mode of passion
persons in the mode of ignorance.

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: nänyaà guëebhyaù kartäraà yadä drañöänupaçyati guëebhyaç ca paraà vetti mad-bhävaà so ’dhigacchati
transliteration: nanyaa gueebhyau kartaraa yada dranoanupacyati gueebhyac ca paraa vetti mad-bhavaa so 'dhigacchati
translation: When you see that there is nothing beyond these modes of nature in all activities and that the Supreme Lord is transcendental to all these modes, then you can know My spiritual nature.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: guëän etän atétya trén dehé deha-samudbhavän janma-måtyu-jarä-duùkhair vimukto ’måtam açnute
transliteration: guean etan atetya tren dehe deha-samudbhavan janma-matyu-jara-duukhair vimukto 'matam acnute
translation: When the embodied being is able to transcend these three modes, he can become free from birth, death, old age and their distresses and can enjoy nectar even in this life.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: arjuna uväca kair liìgais trén guëän etän atéto bhavati prabho kim äcäraù kathaà caitäàs trén guëän ativartate
transliteration: arjuna uvaca kair liigais tren guean etan ateto bhavati prabho kim acarau kathaa caitaas tren guean ativartate
translation: Arjuna inquired: O my dear Lord, by what symptoms is one known who is transcendental to those modes? What is his behavior? And how does he transcend the modes of nature?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: çré-bhagavän uväca prakäçaà ca pravåttià ca moham eva ca päëòava na dveñöi sampravåttäni na nivåttäni käìkñati
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca prakacaa ca pravattia ca moham eva ca paeoava na dvenoi sampravattani na nivattani kaiknati
translation: The Blessed Lord said: He who does not hate illumination, attachment and delusion when they are present, nor longs for them when they disappear; who is seated like one unconcerned, being situated beyond these material reactions of the modes of nature, who remains firm, knowing that the modes alone are active; who regards alike pleasure and pain, and looks on a clod, a stone and a piece of gold with an equal eye; who is wise and holds praise and blame to be the same; who is unchanged in honor and dishonor, who treats friend and foe alike, who has abandoned all fruitive undertakings—such a man is said to have transcended the modes of nature.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: udäséna-vad äséno guëair yo na vicälyate guëä vartanta ity evaà yo ’vatiñöhati neìgate
transliteration: udasena-vad aseno gueair yo na vicalyate guea vartanta ity evaa yo 'vatinohati neigate
translation: The Blessed Lord said: He who does not hate illumination, attachment and delusion when they are present, nor longs for them when they disappear; who is seated like one unconcerned, being situated beyond these material reactions of the modes of nature, who remains firm, knowing that the modes alone are active; who regards alike pleasure and pain, and looks on a clod, a stone and a piece of gold with an equal eye; who is wise and holds praise and blame to be the same; who is unchanged in honor and dishonor, who treats friend and foe alike, who has abandoned all fruitive undertakings—such a man is said to have transcended the modes of nature.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: sama-duùkha-sukhaù sva-sthaù sama-loñöäçma-käïcanaù tulya-priyäpriyo dhéras tulya-nindätma-saàstutiù
transliteration: sama-duukha-sukhau sva-sthau sama-lonoacma-kaicanau tulya-priyapriyo dheras tulya-nindatma-saastutiu
translation: The Blessed Lord said: He who does not hate illumination, attachment and delusion when they are present, nor longs for them when they disappear; who is seated like one unconcerned, being situated beyond these material reactions of the modes of nature, who remains firm, knowing that the modes alone are active; who regards alike pleasure and pain, and looks on a clod, a stone and a piece of gold with an equal eye; who is wise and holds praise and blame to be the same; who is unchanged in honor and dishonor, who treats friend and foe alike, who has abandoned all fruitive undertakings—such a man is said to have transcended the modes of nature.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: mänäpamänayos tulyas tulyo miträri-pakñayoù sarvärambha-parityägé guëätétaù sa ucyate
transliteration: manapamanayos tulyas tulyo mitrari-paknayou sarvarambha-parityage gueatetau sa ucyate
translation: The Blessed Lord said: He who does not hate illumination, attachment and delusion when they are present, nor longs for them when they disappear; who is seated like one unconcerned, being situated beyond these material reactions of the modes of nature, who remains firm, knowing that the modes alone are active; who regards alike pleasure and pain, and looks on a clod, a stone and a piece of gold with an equal eye; who is wise and holds praise and blame to be the same; who is unchanged in honor and dishonor, who treats friend and foe alike, who has abandoned all fruitive undertakings—such a man is said to have transcended the modes of nature.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: mäà ca yo ’vyabhicäreëa bhakti-yogena sevate sa guëän samatétyaitän brahma-bhüyäya kalpate
transliteration: maa ca yo 'vyabhicareea bhakti-yogena sevate sa guean samatetyaitan brahma-bhuyaya kalpate
translation: One who engages in full devotional service, who does not fall down in any circumstance, at once transcends the modes of material nature and thus comes to the level of Brahman.

glossary.gloss: all the modes of material nature
to be elevated on the Brahman platform

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
iast: brahmaëo hi pratiñöhäham amåtasyävyayasya ca çäçvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikäntikasya ca
transliteration: brahmaeo hi pratinohaham amatasyavyayasya ca cacvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikantikasya ca
translation: And I am the basis of the impersonal Brahman, which is the constitutional position of ultimate happiness, and which is immortal, imperishable and eternal.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: çré-bhagavän uväca ürdhva-mülam adhaù-çäkham açvatthaà prähur avyayam chandäàsi yasya parëäni yas taà veda sa veda-vit
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca urdhva-mulam adhau-cakham acvatthaa prahur avyayam chandaasi yasya pareani yas taa veda sa veda-vit
translation: The Blessed Lord said: There is a banyan tree which has its roots upward and its branches down and whose leaves are the Vedic hymns. One who knows this tree is the knower of the Vedas.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: adhaç cordhvaà prasåtäs tasya çäkhä guëa-pravåddhä viñaya-praväläù adhaç ca müläny anusantatäni karmänubandhéni manuñya-loke
transliteration: adhac cordhvaa prasatas tasya cakha guea-pravaddha vinaya-pravalau adhac ca mulany anusantatani karmanubandheni manunya-loke
translation: The branches of this tree extend downward and upward, nourished by the three modes of material nature. The twigs are the objects of the senses. This tree also has roots going down, and these are bound to the fruitive actions of human society.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: na rüpam asyeha tathopalabhyate nänto na cädir na ca sampratiñöhä açvattham enaà su-virüòha-mülam asaìga-çastreëa dåòhena chittvä
transliteration: na rupam asyeha tathopalabhyate nanto na cadir na ca sampratinoha acvattham enaa su-viruoha-mulam asaiga-castreea daohena chittva
translation: The real form of this tree cannot be perceived in this world. No one can understand where it ends, where it begins, or where its foundation is. But with determination one must cut down this tree with the weapon of detachment. So doing, one must seek that place from which, having once gone, one never returns, and there surrender to that Supreme Personality of Godhead from whom everything has begun and in whom everything is abiding since time immemorial.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: tataù padaà tat parimärgitavyaà yasmin gatä na nivartanti bhüyaù tam eva cädyaà puruñaà prapadye yataù pravåttiù prasåtä puräëé
transliteration: tatau padaa tat parimargitavyaa yasmin gata na nivartanti bhuyau tam eva cadyaa purunaa prapadye yatau pravattiu prasata puraee
translation: The real form of this tree cannot be perceived in this world. No one can understand where it ends, where it begins, or where its foundation is. But with determination one must cut down this tree with the weapon of detachment. So doing, one must seek that place from which, having once gone, one never returns, and there surrender to that Supreme Personality of Godhead from whom everything has begun and in whom everything is abiding since time immemorial.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: nirmäna-mohä jita-saìga-doñä adhyätma-nityä vinivåtta-kämäù dvandvair vimuktäù sukha-duùkha-saàjïair gacchanty amüòhäù padam avyayaà tat
transliteration: nirmana-moha jita-saiga-dona adhyatma-nitya vinivatta-kamau dvandvair vimuktau sukha-duukha-saajiair gacchanty amuohau padam avyayaa tat
translation: One who is free from illusion, false prestige, and false association, who understands the eternal, who is done with material lust and is freed from the duality of happiness and distress, and who knows how to surrender unto the Supreme Person, attains to that eternal kingdom.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: na tad bhäsayate süryo na çaçäìko na pävakaù yad gatvä na nivartante tad dhäma paramaà mama
transliteration: na tad bhasayate suryo na cacaiko na pavakau yad gatva na nivartante tad dhama paramaa mama
translation: That abode of Mine is not illumined by the sun or moon, nor by electricity. One who reaches it never returns to this material world.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: mamaiväàço jéva-loke jéva-bhütaù sanätanaù manaù-ñañöhänéndriyäëi prakåti-sthäni karñati
transliteration: mamaivaaco jeva-loke jeva-bhutau sanatanau manau-nanohanendriyaei prakati-sthani karnati
translation: The living entities in this conditioned world are My eternal, fragmental parts. Due to conditioned life, they are struggling very hard with the six senses, which include the mind.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: çaréraà yad aväpnoti yac cäpy utkrämatéçvaraù gåhétvaitäni saàyäti väyur gandhän iväçayät
transliteration: careraa yad avapnoti yac capy utkramatecvarau gahetvaitani saayati vayur gandhan ivacayat
translation: The living entity in the material world carries his different conceptions of life from one body to another as the air carries aromas.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: çrotraà cakñuù sparçanaà ca rasanaà ghräëam eva ca adhiñöhäya manaç cäyaà viñayän upasevate
transliteration: crotraa caknuu sparcanaa ca rasanaa ghraeam eva ca adhinohaya manac cayaa vinayan upasevate
translation: The living entity, thus taking another gross body, obtains a certain type of ear, tongue, and nose and sense of touch, which are grouped about the mind. He thus enjoys a particular set of sense objects.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: utkrämantaà sthitaà väpi bhuïjänaà vä guëänvitam vimüòhä nänupaçyanti paçyanti jïäna-cakñuñaù
transliteration: utkramantaa sthitaa vapi bhuijanaa va gueanvitam vimuoha nanupacyanti pacyanti jiana-caknunau
translation: The foolish cannot understand how a living entity can quit his body, nor can they understand what sort of body he enjoys under the spell of the modes of nature. But one whose eyes are trained in knowledge can see all this.

glossary.gloss: under the spell of the modes of material nature
one who has the eyes of knowledge.

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: yatanto yoginaç cainaà paçyanty ätmany avasthitam yatanto ’py akåtätmäno nainaà paçyanty acetasaù
transliteration: yatanto yoginac cainaa pacyanty atmany avasthitam yatanto 'py akatatmano nainaa pacyanty acetasau
translation: The endeavoring transcendentalist, who is situated in self-realization, can see all this clearly. But those who are not situated in self-realization cannot see what is taking place, though they may try to.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: yad äditya-gataà tejo jagad bhäsayate ’khilam yac candramasi yac cägnau tat tejo viddhi mämakam
transliteration: yad aditya-gataa tejo jagad bhasayate 'khilam yac candramasi yac cagnau tat tejo viddhi mamakam
translation: The splendor of the sun, which dissipates the darkness of this whole world, comes from Me. And the splendor of the moon and the splendor of fire are also from Me.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: gäm äviçya ca bhütäni dhärayämy aham ojasä puñëämi cauñadhéù sarväù somo bhütvä rasätmakaù
transliteration: gam avicya ca bhutani dharayamy aham ojasa puneami caunadheu sarvau somo bhutva rasatmakau
translation: I enter into each planet, and by My energy they stay in orbit. I become the moon and thereby supply the juice of life to all vegetables.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: ahaà vaiçvänaro bhütvä präëinäà deham äçritaù präëäpäna-samäyuktaù pacämy annaà catur-vidham
transliteration: ahaa vaicvanaro bhutva praeinaa deham acritau praeapana-samayuktau pacamy annaa catur-vidham
translation: I am the fire of digestion in every living body, and I am the air of life, outgoing and incoming, by which I digest the four kinds of foodstuff.

glossary.gloss: by My plenary portion as the digesting fire

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: sarvasya cähaà hådi sanniviñöo mattaù småtir jïänam apohanaà ca vedaiç ca sarvair aham eva vedyo vedänta-kåd veda-vid eva cäham
transliteration: sarvasya cahaa hadi sannivinoo mattau smatir jianam apohanaa ca vedaic ca sarvair aham eva vedyo vedanta-kad veda-vid eva caham
translation: I am seated in everyone’s heart, and from Me come remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness. By all the Vedas am I to be known; indeed I am the compiler of Vedänta, and I am the knower of the Vedas.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: dväv imau puruñau loke kñaraç cäkñara eva ca kñaraù sarväëi bhütäni küöa-stho ’kñara ucyate
transliteration: dvav imau purunau loke knarac caknara eva ca knarau sarvaei bhutani kuoa-stho 'knara ucyate
translation: There are two classes of beings, the fallible and the infallible. In the material world every entity is fallible, and in the spiritual world every entity is called infallible.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: uttamaù puruñas tv anyaù paramätmety udähåtaù yo loka-trayam äviçya bibharty avyaya éçvaraù
transliteration: uttamau purunas tv anyau paramatmety udahatau yo loka-trayam avicya bibharty avyaya ecvarau
translation: Besides these two, there is the greatest living personality, the Lord Himself, who has entered into these worlds and is maintaining them.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: yasmät kñaram atéto ’ham akñaräd api cottamaù ato ’smi loke vede ca prathitaù puruñottamaù
transliteration: yasmat knaram ateto 'ham aknarad api cottamau ato 'smi loke vede ca prathitau purunottamau
translation: Because I am transcendental, beyond both the fallible and the infallible, and because I am the greatest, I am celebrated both in the world and in the Vedas as that Supreme Person.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: yo mäm evam asammüòho jänäti puruñottamam sa sarva-vid bhajati mäà sarva-bhävena bhärata
transliteration: yo mam evam asammuoho janati purunottamam sa sarva-vid bhajati maa sarva-bhavena bharata
translation: Whoever knows Me as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, without doubting, is to be understood as the knower of everything, and he therefore engages himself in full devotional service, O son of Bharata
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

chapter_title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
iast: iti guhyatamaà çästram idam uktaà mayänagha etad buddhvä buddhimän syät kåta-kåtyaç ca bhärata
transliteration: iti guhyatamaa castram idam uktaa mayanagha etad buddhva buddhiman syat kata-katyac ca bharata
translation: This is the most confidential part of the Vedic scriptures, O sinless one, and it is disclosed now by Me. Whoever understands this will become wise, and his endeavors will know perfection.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çré-bhagavän uväca abhayaà sattva-saàçuddhir jïäna-yoga-vyavasthitiù dänaà damaç ca yajïaç ca svädhyäyas tapa ärjavam
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca abhayaa sattva-saacuddhir jiana-yoga-vyavasthitiu danaa damac ca yajiac ca svadhyayas tapa arjavam
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purification of one’s existence, cultivation of spiritual knowledge, charity, self-control, performance of sacrifice, study of the Vedas, austerity and simplicity; nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger; renunciation, tranquility, aversion to faultfinding, compassion and freedom from covetousness; gentleness, modesty and steady determination; vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, freedom from envy and the passion for honor—these transcendental qualities, O son of Bharata, belong to godly men endowed with divine nature.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: ahiàsä satyam akrodhas tyägaù çäntir apaiçunam dayä bhüteñv aloluptvaà märdavaà hrér acäpalam
transliteration: ahiasa satyam akrodhas tyagau cantir apaicunam daya bhutenv aloluptvaa mardavaa hrer acapalam
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purification of one’s existence, cultivation of spiritual knowledge, charity, self-control, performance of sacrifice, study of the Vedas, austerity and simplicity; nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger; renunciation, tranquility, aversion to faultfinding, compassion and freedom from covetousness; gentleness, modesty and steady determination; vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, freedom from envy and the passion for honor—these transcendental qualities, O son of Bharata, belong to godly men endowed with divine nature.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tejaù kñamä dhåtiù çaucam adroho näti-mänitä bhavanti sampadaà daivém abhijätasya bhärata
transliteration: tejau knama dhatiu caucam adroho nati-manita bhavanti sampadaa daivem abhijatasya bharata
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purification of one’s existence, cultivation of spiritual knowledge, charity, self-control, performance of sacrifice, study of the Vedas, austerity and simplicity; nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger; renunciation, tranquility, aversion to faultfinding, compassion and freedom from covetousness; gentleness, modesty and steady determination; vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, freedom from envy and the passion for honor—these transcendental qualities, O son of Bharata, belong to godly men endowed with divine nature.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: dambho darpo ’bhimänaç ca krodhaù päruñyam eva ca ajïänaà cäbhijätasya pärtha sampadam äsurém
transliteration: dambho darpo 'bhimanac ca krodhau parunyam eva ca ajianaa cabhijatasya partha sampadam asurem
translation: Arrogance, pride, anger, conceit, harshness and ignorance—these qualities belong to those of demonic nature, O son of Påthä.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: daivé sampad vimokñäya nibandhäyäsuré matä mä çucaù sampadaà daivém abhijäto ’si päëòava
transliteration: daive sampad vimoknaya nibandhayasure mata ma cucau sampadaa daivem abhijato 'si paeoava
translation: The transcendental qualities are conducive to liberation, whereas the demonic qualities make for bondage. Do not worry, O son of Päëòu, for you are born with the divine qualities.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: dvau bhüta-sargau loke ’smin daiva äsura eva ca daivo vistaraçaù prokta äsuraà pärtha me çåëu
transliteration: dvau bhuta-sargau loke 'smin daiva asura eva ca daivo vistaracau prokta asuraa partha me caeu
translation: O son of Påthä, in this world there are two kinds of created beings. One is called the divine and the other demonic. I have already explained to you at length the divine qualities. Now hear from Me of the demoniac.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: pravåttià ca nivåttià ca janä na vidur äsuräù na çaucaà näpi cäcäro na satyaà teñu vidyate
transliteration: pravattia ca nivattia ca jana na vidur asurau na caucaa napi cacaro na satyaa tenu vidyate
translation: Those who are demoniac do not know what is to be done and what is not to be done. Neither cleanliness nor proper behavior nor truth is found in them.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: asatyam apratiñöhaà te jagad ähur anéçvaram aparaspara-sambhütaà kim anyat käma-haitukam
transliteration: asatyam apratinohaa te jagad ahur anecvaram aparaspara-sambhutaa kim anyat kama-haitukam
translation: They say that this world is unreal, that there is no foundation and that there is no God in control. It is produced of sex desire, and has no cause other than lust.

glossary.gloss: it is due to lust only.

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: etäà dåñöim avañöabhya nañöätmäno ’lpa-buddhayaù prabhavanty ugra-karmäëaù kñayäya jagato ’hitäù
transliteration: etaa danoim avanoabhya nanoatmano 'lpa-buddhayau prabhavanty ugra-karmaeau knayaya jagato 'hitau
translation: Following such conclusions, the demoniac, who are lost to themselves and who have no intelligence, engage in unbeneficial, horrible works meant to destroy the world.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: kämam äçritya duñpüraà dambha-mäna-madänvitäù mohäd gåhétväsad-grähän pravartante ’çuci-vratäù
transliteration: kamam acritya dunpuraa dambha-mana-madanvitau mohad gahetvasad-grahan pravartante 'cuci-vratau
translation: The demoniac, taking shelter of insatiable lust, pride and false prestige, and being thus illusioned, are always sworn to unclean work, attracted by the impermanent.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: cintäm aparimeyäà ca pralayäntäm upäçritäù kämopabhoga-paramä etävad iti niçcitäù
transliteration: cintam aparimeyaa ca pralayantam upacritau kamopabhoga-parama etavad iti niccitau
translation: They believe that to gratify the senses unto the end of life is the prime necessity of human civilization. Thus there is no end to their anxiety. Being bound by hundreds and thousands of desires, by lust and anger, they secure money by illegal means for sense gratification.

glossary.gloss: entanglement in the network of hope

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: äçä-päça-çatair baddhäù käma-krodha-paräyaëäù éhante käma-bhogärtham anyäyenärtha-saïcayän
transliteration: aca-paca-catair baddhau kama-krodha-parayaeau ehante kama-bhogartham anyayenartha-saicayan
translation: They believe that to gratify the senses unto the end of life is the prime necessity of human civilization. Thus there is no end to their anxiety. Being bound by hundreds and thousands of desires, by lust and anger, they secure money by illegal means for sense gratification.

glossary.gloss: entanglement in the network of hope

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: idam adya mayä labdham imaà präpsye manoratham idam astédam api me bhaviñyati punar dhanam
transliteration: idam adya maya labdham imaa prapsye manoratham idam astedam api me bhavinyati punar dhanam
translation: The demoniac person thinks: “So much wealth do I have today, and I will gain more according to my schemes. So much is mine now, and it will increase in the future, more and more. He is my enemy, and I have killed him; and my other enemy will also be killed. I am the lord of everything, I am the enjoyer, I am perfect, powerful and happy. I am the richest man, surrounded by aristocratic relatives. There is none so powerful and happy as I am. I shall perform sacrifices, I shall give some charity, and thus I shall rejoice.” In this way, such persons are deluded by ignorance.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: asau mayä hataù çatrur haniñye cäparän api éçvaro ’ham ahaà bhogé siddho ’haà balavän sukhé
transliteration: asau maya hatau catrur haninye caparan api ecvaro 'ham ahaa bhoge siddho 'haa balavan sukhe
translation: The demoniac person thinks: “So much wealth do I have today, and I will gain more according to my schemes. So much is mine now, and it will increase in the future, more and more. He is my enemy, and I have killed him; and my other enemy will also be killed. I am the lord of everything, I am the enjoyer, I am perfect, powerful and happy. I am the richest man, surrounded by aristocratic relatives. There is none so powerful and happy as I am. I shall perform sacrifices, I shall give some charity, and thus I shall rejoice.” In this way, such persons are deluded by ignorance.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: äòhyo ’bhijanavän asmi ko ’nyo ’sti sadåço mayä yakñye däsyämi modiñya ity ajïäna-vimohitäù
transliteration: aohyo 'bhijanavan asmi ko 'nyo 'sti sadaco maya yaknye dasyami modinya ity ajiana-vimohitau
translation: The demoniac person thinks: “So much wealth do I have today, and I will gain more according to my schemes. So much is mine now, and it will increase in the future, more and more. He is my enemy, and I have killed him; and my other enemy will also be killed. I am the lord of everything, I am the enjoyer, I am perfect, powerful and happy. I am the richest man, surrounded by aristocratic relatives. There is none so powerful and happy as I am. I shall perform sacrifices, I shall give some charity, and thus I shall rejoice.” In this way, such persons are deluded by ignorance.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: aneka-citta-vibhräntä moha-jäla-samävåtäù prasaktäù käma-bhogeñu patanti narake ’çucau
transliteration: aneka-citta-vibhranta moha-jala-samavatau prasaktau kama-bhogenu patanti narake 'cucau
translation: Thus perplexed by various anxieties and bound by a network of illusions, one becomes too strongly attached to sense enjoyment and falls down into hell.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: ätma-sambhävitäù stabdhä dhana-mäna-madänvitäù yajante näma-yajïais te dambhenävidhi-pürvakam
transliteration: atma-sambhavitau stabdha dhana-mana-madanvitau yajante nama-yajiais te dambhenavidhi-purvakam
translation: Self-complacent and always impudent, deluded by wealth and false prestige, they sometimes perform sacrifices in name only without following any rules or regulations.

glossary.gloss: without following any rules and regulations.

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: ahaìkäraà balaà darpaà kämaà krodhaà ca saàçritäù mäm ätma-para-deheñu pradviñanto ’bhyasüyakäù
transliteration: ahaikaraa balaa darpaa kamaa krodhaa ca saacritau mam atma-para-dehenu pradvinanto 'bhyasuyakau
translation: Bewildered by false ego, strength, pride, lust and anger, the demon becomes envious of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is situated in his own body and in the bodies of others, and blasphemes against the real religion.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tän ahaà dviñataù krürän saàsäreñu narädhamän kñipämy ajasram açubhän äsuréñv eva yoniñu
transliteration: tan ahaa dvinatau kruran saasarenu naradhaman knipamy ajasram acubhan asurenv eva yoninu
translation: Those who are envious and mischievous, who are the lowest among men, are cast by Me into the ocean of material existence, into various demoniac species of life.

glossary.gloss: into the ocean of material existence

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: äsuréà yonim äpannä müòhä janmani janmani mäm apräpyaiva kaunteya tato yänty adhamäà gatim
transliteration: asurea yonim apanna muoha janmani janmani mam aprapyaiva kaunteya tato yanty adhamaa gatim
translation: Attaining repeated birth amongst the species of demoniac life, such persons can never approach Me. Gradually they sink down to the most abominable type of existence.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tri-vidhaà narakasyedaà dväraà näçanam ätmanaù kämaù krodhas tathä lobhas tasmäd etat trayaà tyajet
transliteration: tri-vidhaa narakasyedaa dvaraa nacanam atmanau kamau krodhas tatha lobhas tasmad etat trayaa tyajet
translation: There are three gates leading to this hell—lust, anger, and greed. Every sane man should give these up, for they lead to the degradation of the soul.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: etair vimuktaù kaunteya tamo-dvärais tribhir naraù äcaraty ätmanaù çreyas tato yäti paräà gatim
transliteration: etair vimuktau kaunteya tamo-dvarais tribhir narau acaraty atmanau creyas tato yati paraa gatim
translation: The man who has escaped these three gates of hell, O son of Kunté, performs acts conducive to self-realization and thus gradually attains the supreme destination.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yaù çästra-vidhim utsåjya vartate käma-kärataù na sa siddhim aväpnoti na sukhaà na paräà gatim
transliteration: yau castra-vidhim utsajya vartate kama-karatau na sa siddhim avapnoti na sukhaa na paraa gatim
translation: But he who discards scriptural injunctions and acts according to his own whims attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme destination.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tasmäc chästraà pramäëaà te käryäkärya-vyavasthitau jïätvä çästra-vidhänoktaà karma kartum ihärhasi
transliteration: tasmac chastraa pramaeaa te karyakarya-vyavasthitau jiatva castra-vidhanoktaa karma kartum iharhasi
translation: One should understand what is duty and what is not duty by the regulations of the scriptures. Knowing such rules and regulations, one should act so that he may gradually be elevated.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: arjuna uväca ye çästra-vidhim utsåjya yajante çraddhayänvitäù teñäà niñöhä tu kä kåñëa sattvam äho rajas tamaù
transliteration: arjuna uvaca ye castra-vidhim utsajya yajante craddhayanvitau tenaa ninoha tu ka kanea sattvam aho rajas tamau
translation: Arjuna said, O Kåñëa, what is the situation of one who does not follow the principles of scripture but worships according to his own imagination? Is he in goodness, in passion or in ignorance?
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çré-bhagavän uväca tri-vidhä bhavati çraddhä dehinäà sä svabhäva-jä sättviké räjasé caiva tämasé ceti täà çåëu
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca tri-vidha bhavati craddha dehinaa sa svabhava-ja sattvike rajase caiva tamase ceti taa caeu
translation: The Supreme Lord said, according to the modes of nature acquired by the embodied soul, one’s faith can be of three kinds—goodness, passion or ignorance. Now hear about these.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said
according to his mode of material nature

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: sattvänurüpä sarvasya çraddhä bhavati bhärata çraddhä-mayo ’yaà puruño yo yac-chraddhaù sa eva saù
transliteration: sattvanurupa sarvasya craddha bhavati bharata craddha-mayo 'yaa puruno yo yac-chraddhau sa eva sau
translation: According to one’s existence under the various modes of nature, one evolves a particular kind of faith. The living being is said to be of a particular faith according to the modes he has acquired.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yajante sättvikä devän yakña-rakñäàsi räjasäù pretän bhüta-gaëäàç cänye yajante tämasä janäù
transliteration: yajante sattvika devan yakna-raknaasi rajasau pretan bhuta-gaeaac canye yajante tamasa janau
translation: Men in the mode of goodness worship the demigods; those in the mode of passion worship the demons; and those in the mode of ignorance worship ghosts and spirits.

glossary.gloss: those who are in the mode of goodness
those who are in the mode of passion worship demons

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: açästra-vihitaà ghoraà tapyante ye tapo janäù dambhähaìkära-saàyuktäù käma-räga-balänvitäù
transliteration: acastra-vihitaa ghoraa tapyante ye tapo janau dambhahaikara-saayuktau kama-raga-balanvitau
translation: Those who undergo severe austerities and penances not recommended in the scriptures, performing them out of pride, egotism, lust and attachment, who are impelled by passion and who torture their bodily organs as well as the Supersoul dwelling within are to be known as demons.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: karñayantaù çaréra-sthaà bhüta-grämam acetasaù mäà caiväntaù çaréra-sthaà tän viddhy äsura-niçcayän
transliteration: karnayantau carera-sthaa bhuta-gramam acetasau maa caivantau carera-sthaa tan viddhy asura-niccayan
translation: Those who undergo severe austerities and penances not recommended in the scriptures, performing them out of pride, egotism, lust and attachment, who are impelled by passion and who torture their bodily organs as well as the Supersoul dwelling within are to be known as demons.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: ähäras tv api sarvasya tri-vidho bhavati priyaù yajïas tapas tathä dänaà teñäà bhedam imaà çåëu
transliteration: aharas tv api sarvasya tri-vidho bhavati priyau yajias tapas tatha danaa tenaa bhedam imaa caeu
translation: Even food of which all partake is of three kinds, according to the three modes of material nature. The same is true of sacrifices, austerities and charity. Listen, and I shall tell you of the distinctions of these.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: äyuù-sattva-balärogyasukha-préti-vivardhanäù rasyäù snigdhäù sthirä hådyä ähäräù sättvika-priyäù
transliteration: ayuu-sattva-balarogyasukha-preti-vivardhanau rasyau snigdhau sthira hadya aharau sattvika-priyau
translation: Foods in the mode of goodness increase the duration of life, purify one’s existence and give strength, health, happiness and satisfaction. Such nourishing foods are sweet, juicy, fattening and palatable.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: kaöv-amla-lavaëäty-uñëatékñëa-rükña-vidähinaù ähärä räjasasyeñöä duùkha-çokämaya-pradäù
transliteration: kaov-amla-lavaeaty-uneateknea-rukna-vidahinau ahara rajasasyenoa duukha-cokamaya-pradau
translation: Foods that are too bitter, too sour, salty, pungent, dry and hot, are liked by people in the modes of passion. Such foods cause pain, distress, and disease.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yäta-yämaà gata-rasaà püti paryuñitaà ca yat ucchiñöam api cämedhyaà bhojanaà tämasa-priyam
transliteration: yata-yamaa gata-rasaa puti paryunitaa ca yat ucchinoam api camedhyaa bhojanaa tamasa-priyam
translation: Food cooked more than three hours before being eaten, which is tasteless, stale, putrid, decomposed and unclean, is food liked by people in the mode of ignorance.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: aphaläkäìkñibhir yajïo vidhi-diñöo ya ijyate yañöavyam eveti manaù samädhäya sa sättvikaù
transliteration: aphalakaiknibhir yajio vidhi-dinoo ya ijyate yanoavyam eveti manau samadhaya sa sattvikau
translation: Of sacrifices, that sacrifice performed according to duty and to scriptural rules, and with no expectation of reward, is of the nature of goodness.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: abhisandhäya tu phalaà dambhärtham api caiva yat ijyate bharata-çreñöha taà yajïaà viddhi räjasam
transliteration: abhisandhaya tu phalaa dambhartham api caiva yat ijyate bharata-crenoha taa yajiaa viddhi rajasam
translation: But that sacrifice performed for some material end or benefit or performed ostentatiously, out of pride, is of the nature of passion, O chief of the Bhäratas.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: vidhi-hénam asåñöännaà mantra-hénam adakñiëam çraddhä-virahitaà yajïaà tämasaà paricakñate
transliteration: vidhi-henam asanoannaa mantra-henam adaknieam craddha-virahitaa yajiaa tamasaa paricaknate
translation: And that sacrifice performed in defiance of scriptural injunctions, in which no spiritual food is distributed, no hymns are chanted and no remunerations are made to the priests, and which is faithless—that sacrifice is of the nature of ignorance.

glossary.gloss: with no chanting of the Vedic hymns
with no remunerations to the priests

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: deva-dvija-guru-präjïapüjanaà çaucam ärjavam brahmacaryam ahiàsä ca çäréraà tapa ucyate
transliteration: deva-dvija-guru-prajiapujanaa caucam arjavam brahmacaryam ahiasa ca careraa tapa ucyate
translation: The austerity of the body consists in this: worship of the Supreme Lord, the brähmaëas, the spiritual master, and superiors like the father and mother. Cleanliness, simplicity, celibacy and nonviolence are also austerities of the body.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: anudvega-karaà väkyaà satyaà priya-hitaà ca yat svädhyäyäbhyasanaà caiva väì-mayaà tapa ucyate
transliteration: anudvega-karaa vakyaa satyaa priya-hitaa ca yat svadhyayabhyasanaa caiva vai-mayaa tapa ucyate
translation: Austerity of speech consists in speaking truthfully and beneficially and in avoiding speech that offends. One should also recite the Vedas regularly.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: manaù-prasädaù saumyatvaà maunam ätma-vinigrahaù bhäva-saàçuddhir ity etat tapo mänasam ucyate
transliteration: manau-prasadau saumyatvaa maunam atma-vinigrahau bhava-saacuddhir ity etat tapo manasam ucyate
translation: And serenity, simplicity, gravity, self-control and purity of thought are the austerities of the mind.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çraddhayä parayä taptaà tapas tat tri-vidhaà naraiù aphaläkäìkñibhir yuktaiù sättvikaà paricakñate
transliteration: craddhaya paraya taptaa tapas tat tri-vidhaa naraiu aphalakaiknibhir yuktaiu sattvikaa paricaknate
translation: This threefold austerity, practiced by men whose aim is not to benefit themselves materially but to please the Supreme, is of the nature of goodness.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: satkära-mäna-püjärthaà tapo dambhena caiva yat kriyate tad iha proktaà räjasaà calam adhruvam
transliteration: satkara-mana-pujarthaa tapo dambhena caiva yat kriyate tad iha proktaa rajasaa calam adhruvam
translation: Those ostentatious penances and austerities which are performed in order to gain respect, honor and reverence are said to be in the mode of passion. They are neither stable nor permanent.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: müòha-gräheëätmano yat péòayä kriyate tapaù parasyotsädanärthaà vä tat tämasam udähåtam
transliteration: muoha-graheeatmano yat peoaya kriyate tapau parasyotsadanarthaa va tat tamasam udahatam
translation: And those penances and austerities which are performed foolishly by means of obstinant self-torture, or to destroy or injure others, are said to be in the mode of ignorance.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: dätavyam iti yad dänaà déyate ’nupakäriëe deçe käle ca pätre ca tad dänaà sättvikaà småtam
transliteration: datavyam iti yad danaa deyate 'nupakariee dece kale ca patre ca tad danaa sattvikaa smatam
translation: That gift which is given out of duty, at the proper time and place, to a worthy person, and without expectation of return, is considered to be charity in the mode of goodness.

glossary.gloss: to any person irrespective of doing good

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yat tu pratyupakärärthaà phalam uddiçya vä punaù déyate ca parikliñöaà tad dänaà räjasaà småtam
transliteration: yat tu pratyupakararthaa phalam uddicya va punau deyate ca pariklinoaa tad danaa rajasaa smatam
translation: But charity performed with the expectation of some return, or with a desire for fruitive results, or in a grudging mood, is said to be charity in the mode of passion.

glossary.gloss: for the sake of getting some return

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: adeça-käle yad dänam apätrebhyaç ca déyate asat-kåtam avajïätaà tat tämasam udähåtam
transliteration: adeca-kale yad danam apatrebhyac ca deyate asat-katam avajiataa tat tamasam udahatam
translation: And charity performed at an improper place and time and given to unworthy persons without respect and with contempt is charity in the mode of ignorance.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: oà tat sad iti nirdeço brahmaëas tri-vidhaù småtaù brähmaëäs tena vedäç ca yajïäç ca vihitäù purä
transliteration: oa tat sad iti nirdeco brahmaeas tri-vidhau smatau brahmaeas tena vedac ca yajiac ca vihitau pura
translation: From the beginning of creation, the three syllables—om tat sat—have been used to indicate the Supreme Absolute Truth [Brahman]. They were uttered by brähmaëas while chanting Vedic hymns and during sacrifices, for the satisfaction of the Supreme.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tasmäd oà ity udähåtya yajïa-däna-tapaù-kriyäù pravartante vidhänoktäù satataà brahma-vädinäm
transliteration: tasmad oa ity udahatya yajia-dana-tapau-kriyau pravartante vidhanoktau satataa brahma-vadinam
translation: Thus the transcendentalists undertake sacrifices, charities, and penances, beginning always with om, to attain the Supreme.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tad ity anabhisandhäya phalaà yajïa-tapaù-kriyäù däna-kriyäç ca vividhäù kriyante mokña-käìkñibhiù
transliteration: tad ity anabhisandhaya phalaa yajia-tapau-kriyau dana-kriyac ca vividhau kriyante mokna-kaiknibhiu
translation: One should perform sacrifice, penance and charity with the word tat. The purpose of such transcendental activities is to get free from the material entanglement.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: sad-bhäve sädhu-bhäve ca sad ity etat prayujyate praçaste karmaëi tathä sac-chabdaù pärtha yujyate
transliteration: sad-bhave sadhu-bhave ca sad ity etat prayujyate pracaste karmaei tatha sac-chabdau partha yujyate
translation: The Absolute Truth is the objective of devotional sacrifice, and it is indicated by the word sat. These works of sacrifice, of penance and of charity, true to the absolute nature, are performed to please the Supreme Person, O son of Påthä.

glossary.gloss: in the sense of the nature of the Supreme
in the sense of the nature of devotion

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yajïe tapasi däne ca sthitiù sad iti cocyate karma caiva tad-arthéyaà sad ity eväbhidhéyate
transliteration: yajie tapasi dane ca sthitiu sad iti cocyate karma caiva tad-artheyaa sad ity evabhidheyate
translation: The Absolute Truth is the objective of devotional sacrifice, and it is indicated by the word sat. These works of sacrifice, of penance and of charity, true to the absolute nature, are performed to please the Supreme Person, O son of Påthä.

glossary.gloss: in the sense of the nature of the Supreme
in the sense of the nature of devotion

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: açraddhayä hutaà dattaà tapas taptaà kåtaà ca yat asad ity ucyate pärtha na ca tat pretya no iha
transliteration: acraddhaya hutaa dattaa tapas taptaa kataa ca yat asad ity ucyate partha na ca tat pretya no iha
translation: But sacrifices, austerities and charities performed without faith in the Supreme are nonpermanent, O son of Påthä, regardless of whatever rites are performed. They are called asat and are useless both in this life and the next.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: arjuna uväca sannyäsasya mahä-bäho tattvam icchämi veditum tyägasya ca håñékeça påthak keçé-niñüdana
transliteration: arjuna uvaca sannyasasya maha-baho tattvam icchami veditum tyagasya ca hanekeca pathak kece-ninudana
translation: Arjuna said, O mighty-armed one, I wish to understand the purpose of renunciation [tyäga] and of the renounced order of life [sannyäsa], O killer of the Keçé demon, Håñékeça.

glossary.gloss: O killer of the Keçé demon.

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: çré-bhagavän uväca kämyänäà karmaëäà nyäsaà sannyäsaà kavayo viduù sarva-karma-phala-tyägaà prähus tyägaà vicakñaëäù
transliteration: cre-bhagavan uvaca kamyanaa karmaeaa nyasaa sannyasaa kavayo viduu sarva-karma-phala-tyagaa prahus tyagaa vicaknaeau
translation: The Supreme Lord said, To give up the results of all activities is called renunciation [tyäga] by the wise. And that state is called the renounced order of life [sannyäsa] by great learned men.

glossary.gloss: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said

source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: tyäjyaà doña-vad ity eke karma prähur manéñiëaù yajïa-däna-tapaù-karma na tyäjyam iti cäpare
transliteration: tyajyaa dona-vad ity eke karma prahur manenieau yajia-dana-tapau-karma na tyajyam iti capare
translation: Some learned men declare that all kinds of fruitive activities should be given up, but there are yet other sages who maintain that acts of sacrifice, charity and penance should never be abandoned.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: niçcayaà çåëu me tatra tyäge bharata-sattama tyägo hi puruña-vyäghra tri-vidhaù samprakértitaù
transliteration: niccayaa caeu me tatra tyage bharata-sattama tyago hi puruna-vyaghra tri-vidhau samprakertitau
translation: O best of the Bhäratas, hear from Me now about renunciation. O tiger among men, there are three kinds of renunciation declared in the scriptures.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: yajïa-däna-tapaù-karma na tyäjyaà käryam eva tat yajïo dänaà tapaç caiva pävanäni manéñiëäm
transliteration: yajia-dana-tapau-karma na tyajyaa karyam eva tat yajio danaa tapac caiva pavanani manenieam
translation: Acts of sacrifice, charity and penance are not to be given up but should be performed. Indeed, sacrifice, charity and penance purify even the great souls.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: etäny api tu karmäëi saìgaà tyaktvä phaläni ca kartavyänéti me pärtha niçcitaà matam uttamam
transliteration: etany api tu karmaei saigaa tyaktva phalani ca kartavyaneti me partha niccitaa matam uttamam
translation: All these activities should be performed without any expectation of result. They should be performed as a matter of duty, O son of Påthä. That is My final opinion.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: niyatasya tu sannyäsaù karmaëo nopapadyate mohät tasya parityägas tämasaù parikértitaù
transliteration: niyatasya tu sannyasau karmaeo nopapadyate mohat tasya parityagas tamasau parikertitau
translation: Prescribed duties should never be renounced. If, by illusion, one gives up his prescribed duties, such renunciation is said to be in the mode of ignorance.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: duùkham ity eva yat karma käya-kleça-bhayät tyajet sa kåtvä räjasaà tyägaà naiva tyäga-phalaà labhet
transliteration: duukham ity eva yat karma kaya-kleca-bhayat tyajet sa katva rajasaa tyagaa naiva tyaga-phalaa labhet
translation: Anyone who gives up prescribed duties as troublesome, or out of fear, is said to be in the mode of passion. Such action never leads to the elevation of renunciation.
source: Bhagavad-gita As It Is verse text

iast: käryam ity eva yat karma niyataà kriyate ’rjuna saìgaà tyaktvä phalaà caiva sa tyägaù sättviko mataù
transliteration: karyam ity eva yat karma niyataa kriyate 'rjuna saigaa tyaktva phalaa caiva sa tyagau sattviko matau
